You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool in the East US region.  
  
You need to implement a disaster recovery solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- If users cannot connect to the Azure Virtual Desktop resources in the East US region, they must be able to connect to equivalent resources in the West US region.  
- Users must connect to the Azure Virtual Desktop resources in either East US or West US by selecting a single icon in the Remote Desktop client.  
- During a disaster, an administrator must initiate failover between the Azure regions manually.  
- Failover times must be minimized.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure a shared image gallery that has replicas in the East US and West US regions
Create new session hosts in the West US region and add the session hosts to an existing host pool
Create an additional host pool in the West US region
Enable Azure Site Recovery replication of the virtual machines to the West US region
Enable Azure Backup to a Recovery Services vault in the West US region

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop can register session-host VMs deployed in a different Azure region with one host pool. Keeping already provisioned West US session hosts in the existing pool retains one published resource for users and allows an administrator to manually direct capacity to the surviving regional hosts, with no wait for VM replication or deployment. A single cross-region host pool is specifically supported for scenarios where duplicate resource definitions and assignments should be avoided.

**Learn more:** [Multiregion BCDR for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/example-scenario/azure-virtual-desktop/azure-virtual-desktop-multi-region-bcdr) · [Add session hosts to a host pool - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/add-session-hosts-host-pool)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop pooled host pool named HostPool1.  
  
You need to dynamically allocate resources to HostPool1 according to the number of sessions on each host.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Desktop scaling plan configures Autoscale for a pooled host pool. It uses host-pool capacity thresholds and session limits to scale session-host resources in response to usage.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop pooled host pool named HostPool1.  
  
You need to dynamically allocate resources to HostPool1 according to the number of sessions on each host.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: a role assignment for the host pool
a role assignment for each virtual machine
a policy preference in a Group Policy Object (GPO)
a device setting in Azure AD

questions.explanation:
A Group Policy Object can use the Local Users and Groups preference extension to manage membership of the local Administrators group on the Active Directory domain-joined session hosts. Adding the Department1 domain group through that preference grants its members local administrator membership on the applicable virtual machines.

**Learn more:** [Local Users and Groups extension](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-R2-and-2012/dn581922(v=ws.11))

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 and an Azure Storage account named Storage1. Storage1 stores FSLogix profile containers in a share folder named share1.  
  
You create a new group named Group1 and grant Group1 permission to sign in to Pool1.  
  
You need to ensure that Group1 members can store FSLogix profile containers in share1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which two privileges should you assign to Group1? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the Storage Blob Data Contributor role for storage1
the List folder / read data NTFS permissions for share1
the Modify NTFS permissions for share1
the Storage File Data SMB Share Reader role for storage1
the Storage File Data SMB Share Elevated Contributor role for storage1
the Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor role for storage1

questions.explanation:
Azure Files requires share-level access and NTFS permissions. Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor provides the required SMB share data access without granting elevated permission-management capabilities. For FSLogix user-based access, the recommended NTFS ACL grants the user group Modify on the share folder only, allowing members to create their own profile directories while CREATOR OWNER permissions protect the contents of those directories from other users.

**Learn more:** [Store FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files and Active Directory Domain Services or Microsoft Entra Domain Services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-container-azure-files-active-directory) · [Configure SMB Storage Permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-storage-permissions)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named `corp.contoso.com`. The domain includes two users named User1 and User2.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named `contoso.com` that contains a user named User3 and synchronizes with `corp.contoso.com`.  
  
The users’ synchronization status is shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783893980470-hix32ie5.png)  
  
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes Microsoft Entra joined session hosts.  
  
You create an Azure Storage account with the following configuration:  
  
- Name: storage1  
- Kind: FileStorage  
- File share: share1  
- Microsoft Entra Kerberos: Enabled  
  
You need to implement FSLogix profile containers on share1.  
  
For which users can you implement a profile container?
questions.explanation:
Azure Files with Microsoft Entra Kerberos supports FSLogix profile containers from Microsoft Entra joined session hosts for hybrid identities and for cloud-only identities (currently preview). User2 is a synchronized hybrid identity, and User3 is a cloud-only Microsoft Entra identity. User1 is not synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID and therefore cannot use this Microsoft Entra-based Azure Virtual Desktop profile-container configuration.

**Learn more:** [Store FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-container-entra-id-hybrid) · [Microsoft Entra joined session hosts in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/azure-ad-joined-session-hosts)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription linked to a hybrid Microsoft Entra tenant that contains a storage account named storage.  
  
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment containing a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has session hosts that are Microsoft Entra joined.  
  
You plan to deploy FSLogix profile containers for Pool1's session hosts.  
  
In storage1, you create a new Azure Files share named share1.  
  
You need to ensure that share1 can store the FSLogix profile containers.  
  
What should you enable for share1?

options.text: a security profile set to Maximum security
a security profile set to Maximum compatibility

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication enables Microsoft Entra joined Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts using hybrid identities to obtain Kerberos tickets for SMB access to an Azure Files share. That access is required for the share to host FSLogix profile containers.

**Learn more:** [Store FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-container-entra-id-hybrid) · [Microsoft Entra joined session hosts in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/azure-ad-joined-session-hosts)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop session host pool containing ten virtual machines.  
  
You need to grant a group of pilot users access to the virtual machines in the pool.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the users to a Remote Desktop Users group on the virtual machines.
Add the users to the local Administrators group on the virtual machines.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop makes desktops and applications available by assigning users or groups to an application group through Azure RBAC. The assignment grants the appropriate Desktop Virtualization User access; no custom role definition or local administrator membership is required.

**Learn more:** [Deploy Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/deploy-azure-virtual-desktop) · [Delegated access in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/delegated-access-virtual-desktop)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an on-premises Active Directory domain containing a universal security group named AVDusers. You also have a hybrid Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant, and AVDusers is synchronized to Azure AD.  
  
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool made up of four Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session hosts.  
  
You need to ensure that only members of AVDusers are able to establish Azure Virtual Desktop sessions to this host pool.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign AVDusers to an Azure role scoped to each host pool.
On each session host, add AVDusers to the local Remote Desktop Users group.
Assign AVDusers to an Azure role scoped to the session hosts.
Assign AVDusers to an application group.

questions.explanation:
In Azure Virtual Desktop, end-user access to a host pool's resources (desktops or RemoteApps) is granted by assigning users or groups to the host pool's application group(s), not through Azure RBAC roles (which govern administrative/management permissions on the host pool or session hosts) and not solely through local Remote Desktop Users group membership. Assigning the AVDusers security group to the application group ensures only its members can see and connect to the published desktop/apps on that host pool, per Microsoft's Azure Virtual Desktop access control model.

**Learn more:** [Manage app groups for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/manage-app-groups) · [Assign users and groups to an app group - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/create-application-group)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. You have determined the network latency between the locations where your users are based and the region where you intend to deploy the environment.  
  
Which tool should you use to determine the best Azure region in which to deploy the host pool?

options.text: Azure Monitor for Azure Virtual Desktop

questions.explanation:
The Azure Virtual Desktop Experience Estimator lets you input a client location and returns the estimated round-trip time (RTT) to each available Azure region, highlighting the region with the lowest latency. This makes it the appropriate tool for selecting the optimal region for a host pool based on end-user network latency, since a lower RTT correlates with a better remote desktop user experience (generally under 100 ms is ideal). Azure Traffic Manager is for routing traffic across deployed endpoints, Azure Monitor for Azure Virtual Desktop is for monitoring an already-deployed environment's performance and health, and Azure Advisor gives general optimization recommendations for existing resources — none of these are designed to estimate regional latency prior to deployment.

**Learn more:** [Analyze connection quality in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/connection-latency) · [Azure Virtual Desktop Experience Estimator](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/virtual-desktop/assessment/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription and an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The subscription includes the storage locations shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783895707814-0bl55uop.png)  
  
You plan to use app attach to deploy an image named `App1.vhdx`.  
  
You need to copy `App1.vhdx` to a storage location.  
  
To which locations can you copy `App1.vhdx`?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop App Attach requires application disk images such as VHDX files to be stored on an SMB file share that session hosts can access. Azure Files provides SMB file shares, whereas Azure Blob Storage containers do not. Therefore, either Azure Files share is suitable, assuming the session hosts have the necessary read permissions.

**Learn more:** [App Attach in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/app-attach-overview) · [Add and manage App Attach applications in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/app-attach-setup)

questions.question:
You need to prepare the disk on VM1 for use in the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Convert the disk format to VHD.
Convert the disk type to Differencing.
Convert the disk type to Fixed size.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Desktop image uploaded from this Generation 1 Hyper-V VM must use the VHD format and a fixed-size disk. VM1 currently uses a dynamically expanding VHDX, so it must be converted to a fixed-size VHD.\
\
**Learn more:** [Prepare a Windows VHD or VHDX to upload to Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/prepare-for-upload-vhd-image) · [Prepare and customize a VHD image of Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-customize-master-image)

questions.question:
You need to prepare the disk on VM1 for use in the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Files Premium provides fully managed SMB file shares backed by solid-state drives, which can store FSLogix profile containers while minimizing operational administration. Azure Files is the recommended storage solution for most Azure Virtual Desktop FSLogix deployments; Premium is the Azure Files tier that satisfies the SSD requirement, whereas Standard file shares are HDD-backed. Azure NetApp Files is appropriate for larger or specialized workloads but has higher provisioning requirements and cost.

**Learn more:** [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile) · [Container storage options for FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-container-storage-options)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. Every session host in Pool1 has only a private IP address assigned.  
  
You need to make sure administrators can remotely connect to the session hosts. The solution must allow administrators to connect to the session hosts by using Azure Command-Line Interface (CLI) and the Remote Desktop client for Windows.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Azure Bastion Standard supports native-client connections to virtual machines with private IP addresses. Administrators can use Azure CLI to initiate RDP with `az network bastion rdp`, which opens the Remote Desktop client on Windows without exposing the session hosts through public IP addresses. Native-client support requires the Bastion Standard SKU or higher.

**Learn more:** [Connect to a VM using Bastion – Windows native client](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/connect-vm-native-client-windows)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment in the East US Azure region and a disaster-recovery location in the West US Azure region.  
  
You need to recommend a disaster recovery solution that fulfills these requirements:  
  
- Controlled failover and failback tests between the two regions must occur every six months.  
- Administrative effort and costs must be kept to a minimum.  
  
What should you recommend?

options.text: Implement an active-active disaster recovery solution.
Back up the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment by using Azure Backup.
Implement an active-passive disaster recovery solution.
Back up the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment by using an Azure Backup vault.

questions.explanation:
An active-passive Azure Virtual Desktop design provides a secondary regional deployment for controlled failover and failback while keeping fewer, or potentially no, compute resources running in the secondary region during normal operation. This reduces operating cost and administrative overhead compared with active-active, which maintains two active host-pool deployments. Azure Backup provides data recovery, not the regional failover and failback capability required for this disaster-recovery strategy.

**Learn more:** [Business continuity considerations for Azure Virtual Desktop workloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/azure-virtual-desktop/business-continuity) · [Business continuity and disaster recovery for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/azure-virtual-desktop/eslz-business-continuity-and-disaster-recovery)

questions.explanation:

What should you use as the application source?

\

questions.question:
Solution: Modify the IP configuration on every session host.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
A session host can make outbound internet connections without having a public IP address. Restricting internet access while allowing the required Azure Virtual Desktop and Microsoft service endpoints requires outbound network filtering, such as Azure Firewall, a network security group, or a proxy configured with the necessary allow rules. Microsoft recommends Azure Firewall to filter Azure Virtual Desktop outbound traffic and documents the required session-host endpoints.\
\
**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites) · [Required FQDNs and endpoints for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/required-fqdn-endpoint)

questions.domain: Plan and implement user environments and apps
questions.question:
Solution: You configure the host pool’s RDP Properties.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop host-pool RDP properties control Remote Desktop Protocol connection and session settings; they do not restrict outbound internet connectivity from session hosts. Outbound user internet access must be controlled through network egress filtering, such as Azure Firewall application and network rules or a proxy, while allowing the required Microsoft service endpoints.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set custom RDP properties on a host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/customize-rdp-properties) · [Use Azure Firewall to protect Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/protect-azure-virtual-desktop)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: You configure rules in the network security group (NSG) that is linked to the subnet containing the session hosts.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Network security groups can be applied at the subnet level containing the AVD session hosts, and their rules can use Azure service tags (such as WindowsVirtualDesktop, AzureCloud, and others) to explicitly permit outbound traffic to required Microsoft services while blocking general outbound internet access via the Internet tag. This satisfies the requirement to prevent general internet access from AVD sessions while still allowing access to necessary Microsoft services, so the solution meets the goal.\
\
**Learn more:** [Required URLs for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/safe-url-list) · [Network security groups overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-groups-overview)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: You configure rules in the network security group (NSG) that is linked to the subnet containing the session hosts.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The virtual network's Address space setting only defines the IP range(s) available for subnets within that VNet; it has no bearing on outbound internet connectivity or traffic filtering. To prevent internet access from AVD sessions while still permitting the required Microsoft service endpoints, you need to control outbound traffic using mechanisms such as Azure Firewall (using the WindowsVirtualDesktop FQDN tag) or Network Security Group rules with appropriate service tags/application rules. Simply modifying the address space does not restrict or filter any traffic, so it does not achieve the goal.

**Learn more:** [Use Azure Firewall to protect Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/protect-azure-virtual-desktop) · [Required FQDNs and endpoints for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/required-fqdn-endpoint)

You need to configure storage for the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment's FSLogix profile containers. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Support FSLogix Profile containers.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
Which storage account should you use for the FSLogix profile containers?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix profile containers can be stored on Azure Files SMB shares. Standard Azure Files shares are deployed in general-purpose v2 (StorageV2) accounts and use pay-as-you-go billing, making a Standard StorageV2 account the cost-minimizing supported choice. Locally redundant storage (LRS) is supported for Azure Files. [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile)

**Learn more:** [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile)

Modify the replication settings of storage1.

questions.explanation:
FSLogix Cloud Cache provides resiliency and high availability for Profile Containers by using a locally mounted cache and periodically updating remote storage providers. It supports profile availability during short-term or intermittent storage issues while using the nearest preferred provider for reads, which supports user performance requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud Cache Overview - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-fslogix-cloud-cache) · [Configuration Settings - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/reference-configuration-settings)

options.text: Assign network security groups (NSGs) to the network interfaces of the five session hosts.
Assign a network security group (NSG) to Subnet1.

questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access uses Network Security Group rules to restrict management ports and temporarily permit approved inbound access. Because all five session hosts are connected to Subnet1, associating an NSG with that subnet applies the required network control to all of them. [Microsoft Learn: Just-in-time machine access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named `corp.contoso.com`.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that synchronizes with `corp.contoso.com`.  
  
You plan to deploy Azure Virtual Desktop.  
  
You need to recommend a user-profile management solution. The solution must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- Support server operating system SKUs.  
- Allow user settings and data to roam.  
- Support cloud-based storage for user profiles.  
- Support Microsoft OneDrive for Business in pooled host pools.  
  
What should be included in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix profile containers provide a complete roaming user profile for Azure Virtual Desktop by dynamically mounting a user-profile VHD/VHDX from supported remote storage, including cloud storage such as Azure Files. They are the recommended Azure Virtual Desktop profile solution for pooled hosts, and they enable OneDrive in non-persistent VDI environments, where OneDrive is otherwise unsupported.

**Learn more:** [User profile management for Azure Virtual Desktop with FSLogix profile containers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/fslogix-profile-containers) · [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment with a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 includes session hosts deployed in a resource group named RG1 and connected to a virtual network subnet named Subnet1.  
  
You create a virtual machine named VM1 with the following configuration:  
  
- It is connected to a subnet named Subnet2.  
- It is deployed to a resource group named RG2.  
- It has the FSLogix agent installed and FSLogix registry keys configured.  
  
You plan to use VM1 to create an image for deploying new session hosts.  
  
You need to ensure that multiple session hosts can be deployed by using the gold image.  
  
What should you do before capturing the image?

options.text: Delete the FSLogix registry keys from VM1.
Uninstall the FSLogix agent from VM1.

questions.explanation:
Generalizing a Windows VM with Sysprep removes machine-specific information and prepares the operating system image to create multiple distinct virtual machines. This is the required preparation for a reusable Azure Virtual Desktop golden image; the source VM's resource group and subnet do not need to match the target session hosts, and FSLogix can be included in the image.

**Learn more:** [Deprovision or generalize a VM before creating an image - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/generalize) · [Create an Azure Virtual Desktop golden image](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-golden-image)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 that includes three session hosts. The session hosts are configured to use FSLogix profiles.  
  
On a management computer, you create an Application Masking rule file and an assignment file.  
  
You need to apply Application Masking to the session hosts in Pool1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the FSLogix agent on the session hosts in Pool1.
Compile the rule and assignment files.
Copy the files to the session hosts in Pool1.

questions.explanation:
FSLogix Application Masking is deployed by copying the Rule Set’s rule and assignment files to each session host, specifically under `C:\Program Files\FSLogix\Apps\Rules`. The FSLogix Apps service processes the files from that location and applies the masking rules.

**Learn more:** [Create and Implement Rule Sets (Application Masking) - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/tutorial-application-rule-sets)

questions.domain: Plan and implement user environments and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com and an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You have a RemoteApp app group called RemoteApp1.  
  
You have a partner company, Fabrikam, Inc., with 200 users. Those users need access to RemoteApp1.  
  
You need to determine the pricing type associated with providing the Fabrikam users access to RemoteApp1.  
  
What should you identify?

options.text: Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access and compute only
Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access only
Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access, compute, storage, and networking

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access pricing provides access rights for external users and is charged in addition to the Azure resources that host the deployment. Those resources incur compute, storage, and networking consumption charges; RemoteApp-only use is billed under the Apps per-user access tier. [Microsoft Learn: Licensing Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/licensing)

**Learn more:** [Licensing Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/licensing) · [Understand and estimate costs for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/understand-estimate-costs)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises network and an Azure subscription. The subscription includes the following virtual network:  
  
- Name: VNet1  
- Address space: 10.10.0.0/16  
- Subnet name: Subnet1  
- Subnet1 address range: 10.10.0.0/16  
  
You deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool containing 10 session hosts to Subnets.  
  
You plan to deploy a VPN gateway to VNet1 and give the session hosts access to the on-premises network.  
  
You need to ensure that the VPN gateway can be deployed.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the address range of Subnet1.
Add a subnet named GatewaySubnet to VNet1.
Modify the address space of VNet1.
Associate a network security group (NSG) to Subnet1.

questions.explanation:
An Azure VPN gateway must be deployed in a dedicated subnet named `GatewaySubnet`. Because `Subnet1` consumes all of VNet1’s `10.10.0.0/16` address space, its range must be modified to reserve a non-overlapping address range for `GatewaySubnet`.

**Learn more:** [Azure VPN Gateway configuration settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-about-vpn-gateway-settings)

You are planning an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that must satisfy the department requirements shown in the table below.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784171702197-z6yct781.png)  
  
You intend to use Azure Virtual Desktop host pools that use load balancing and autoscaling.  
  
You need to design a host pool configuration that satisfies the requirements while minimizing costs.  
  
What is the minimum number of host pools you should recommend?
questions.explanation:
All session hosts within a single Azure Virtual Desktop host pool must share the same configuration (VM size/SKU, GPU vs. non-GPU, and single-session vs. multi-session/personal vs. pooled), since a host pool represents session hosts serving the same workload. Research's requirement for a single-session (personal) desktop with no GPU cannot share a host pool with any pooled workload, so it requires its own host pool. Engineering's requirement for a multi-session desktop with GPU support requires GPU-enabled session hosts, which differs from the non-GPU session hosts needed by IT and Finance, so Engineering also needs a dedicated host pool. IT's multi-session desktop requirement and Finance's RemoteApp requirement both call for non-GPU, multi-session session hosts with identical specifications; because a single pooled host pool can support both a Desktop application group and a RemoteApp application group at the same time, IT and Finance can share one host pool, assigning IT users to the Desktop application group and Finance users to the RemoteApp application group. This results in a minimum of three host pools: one for Research (personal/single-session, no GPU), one for Engineering (pooled/multi-session, GPU), and one shared by IT and Finance (pooled/multi-session, no GPU, with separate application groups).

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Desktop terminology](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/terminology) · [Host pool management approaches - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/host-pool-management-approaches)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 and a user named User1. Pool1 includes two session hosts named Host1 and Host2. The deployment uses FSLogix profile containers stored in Azure Files. The image used for all session hosts has an app named App1 installed.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can launch App1 only when connecting to Host1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Use FSLogix application masking.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: On Host2, create an Application Rule Set that masks App1.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a Conditional Access policy.
On Host1, create an Application Rule Set that masks App1.

questions.explanation:
An FSLogix Application Rule Set can use hiding rules to make an installed application unavailable to an assigned user on a specific session host. Masking App1 on Host2 prevents User1 from launching it there while leaving the application available on Host1. Conditional Access and FSLogix profile-container exclusions do not provide application masking.

**Learn more:** [FSLogix Apps RuleEditor and Rule Sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-fslogix-apps-rule-editor-rule-sets) · [Create and Implement Rule Sets (Application Masking)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/tutorial-application-rule-sets)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The deployment has a host pool named Pool.  
  
Users access the deployment using the Windows client for Azure Virtual Desktop.  
  
You need to ensure that users must reauthenticate every eight hours. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a Conditional Access policy.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, configure the User settings.
Define Pool1 as a validation environment.
For each session host, configure just-in-time (JIT) VM access.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can apply a sign-in-frequency session control to Azure Virtual Desktop. Setting periodic reauthentication to eight hours centrally requires users to authenticate again when a new access token is required, without configuring each session host individually.

**Learn more:** [Enforce Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication for Azure Virtual Desktop using Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-mfa)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool.  
  
The host pool has 100 session hosts running Windows 11 on general-purpose virtual machines.  
  
You plan to implement Quality of Service (QoS) for the deployment.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Switch to a compute optimized virtual machine.
Switch to a high-performance computing (HPC) virtual machine.

questions.explanation:
RDP Shortpath for managed networks provides the direct UDP-based RDP transport that enables QoS policies and DSCP marking for Azure Virtual Desktop RDP traffic. A scaling plan manages session-host availability, while changing to compute-optimized or HPC virtual machines does not configure network traffic prioritization.

options.text: Configure the international settings on each host

Apply a Group Policy setting to disable the Time & language settings
Apply a Group Policy setting that blocks the cleanup of unused language packs

questions.explanation:

You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and the storage accounts shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783878888102-yuaeqxif.png)  
  
You plan to deploy a host pool named Pool1 in the East US Azure region. Pool1 will use FSLogix Profile Containers and Office Containers.  
  
Which storage accounts can Pool1 use?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix Profile Containers and Office Containers are stored on SMB file shares. StorageV2 supports standard Azure Files shares, and FileStorage supports premium Azure Files shares; BlobBlockStorage does not provide Azure Files SMB shares. Container storage should be deployed in the same region as the Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts to minimize latency, so the East US accounts storage1 and storage2 can be used.

**Learn more:** [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile) · [Container storage options for FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-container-storage-options)

Which settings should you configure to satisfy the performance requirements?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783895711274-2o2y7h7l.png)

options.text: Load balancing for each session host
Scaling plan for the host pool

questions.explanation:
A pooled Azure Virtual Desktop host pool uses depth-first load balancing to place new sessions on one session host until it reaches its maximum session limit, then directs sessions to the next host. The load-balancing algorithm and a maximum session limit of 15 are configured in the host pool properties.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure host pool load balancing in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-load-balancing)

questions.explanation:
Azure NetApp Files can create Active Directory-integrated SMB volumes, enabling access control with on-premises Active Directory users and groups. For Azure Virtual Desktop FSLogix containers, Azure NetApp Files offers substantially higher IOPS and lower latency than Azure Files, making it the appropriate choice when read and write performance must be maximized.

**Learn more:** [Store FSLogix profile containers for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile) · [Benefits of using Azure NetApp Files with Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-netapp-files/solutions-windows-virtual-desktop)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You use Hyper-V to create a virtual machine running Windows 10 with these configurations:  
  
- Virtual machine generation: Generation 1  
- Disk type: Dynamically expanding  
- Disk format: VHDX  
- Disk size: 2 TB  
  
You need to prepare the virtual machine before you upload it to Azure.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Change the disk type to fixed.
Decrease the disk size to 1 TB.
Change the disk format to VHD.
Change the disk type to differencing.
Change the virtual machine generation to generation 2.

questions.explanation:
Azure supports Generation 1 and Generation 2 VMs for upload when the OS disk is a fixed-size VHD. A dynamically expanding VHDX must therefore be converted to a fixed VHD. A 2-TB OS VHD is within the maximum supported size for a Generation 1 VM, so resizing and changing generation are unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Prepare a Windows VHD or VHDX to upload to Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/prepare-for-upload-vhd-image)

You need to monitor the deployment by using the Azure Virtual Desktop Insights solution in Azure Monitor.  
  
Which Diagnostic settings destination should you use for the host pool?

You need to make sure that administrators can start an RDP session to the session hosts through the Azure portal.  
  
What should you implement?

options.text: Remote Desktop Connection Broker (RD Connection Broker)
Remote Desktop Session Host (RD Session Host)

questions.explanation:
Azure Bastion provides secure, browser-based RDP access from the Azure portal to virtual machines using their private IP addresses, so the session hosts do not need public IP addresses or publicly exposed RDP ports.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create an RDP connection to a Windows VM using Azure Bastion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/bastion-connect-vm-rdp-windows) · [Quickstart: Deploy Azure Bastion from the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/quickstart-host-portal)

questions.question:
You deploy several Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts that have only private IP addresses.  
  
You need to make sure that administrators can start an RDP session to the session hosts through the Azure portal.  
  
What should you implement?

options.text: Regenerate the token and reregister the virtual machines in the host pools.
Create two new host pools in the West US region.
Create an Azure Site Recovery plan.

questions.explanation:
An active-passive Azure Virtual Desktop disaster recovery design can use Azure Site Recovery for both personal (dedicated) and pooled (shared) host pools while maintaining a single host pool entity. Azure Site Recovery replicates the session-host virtual machines to the recovery region and a recovery plan orchestrates their failover, avoiding the added infrastructure and management of separate secondary host pools.

**Learn more:** [Business continuity and disaster recovery for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/azure-virtual-desktop/eslz-business-continuity-and-disaster-recovery) · [Tutorial: Set up disaster recovery for Azure VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/site-recovery/azure-to-azure-tutorial-enable-replication)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 that includes the following:  
  
- A linked workspace named Workspace1  
- An application group named Default Desktop  
- A session host named Host1  
  
You need to add a new data disk.  
  
What should you modify?
questions.explanation:
A session host in Azure Virtual Desktop is an Azure virtual machine. Disks (including data disks) are a property of the VM resource itself, so to add a new data disk you must modify the session host (Host1) VM in Azure, not the host pool, workspace, or application group, which govern connection and publishing settings rather than VM storage configuration.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/terminology) · [Add a data disk to a Windows VM - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/attach-managed-disk-portal)

You need to create a PowerShell script that signs users out of a particular session host before you perform a maintenance task.  
  
Which PowerShell module should you load in the script?
questions.explanation:
The `Az.DesktopVirtualization` module provides Azure Virtual Desktop user-session cmdlets, including `Disconnect-AzWvdUserSession`, which disconnects a user session from a specified session host.\
\
**Learn more:** [Disconnect-AzWvdUserSession (Az.DesktopVirtualization)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.desktopvirtualization/disconnect-azwvdusersession?view=azps-15.3.0) · [Use Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell with Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/cli-powershell)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment containing multiple host pools.  
  
You need to create a PowerShell script that signs users out of a particular session host before you perform a maintenance task.  
  
Which PowerShell module should you load in the script?

options.text: Add Admin1 to the AAD DC Administrators group of contoso.com.
Assign the Cloud device administrator role to Admin1.
Assign a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 license to Admin1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Domain Services (Azure AD DS) requires that NTLM and Kerberos password hashes be present for a user account before that account can authenticate against the managed domain, for example to join a session host VM to it. These hashes are only generated and synchronized into Azure AD DS when the user's password is set or changed after Azure AD DS has been provisioned. Because Admin1's password was already set prior to enabling Azure AD DS, its hash is not yet available in the managed domain, so a password change is required first to enable Admin1 to authenticate and join the Windows 10 Enterprise session hosts to Pool1's Azure AD DS domain.

**Learn more:** [Entra Domain Services and Windows AD Password Hash Synchronization - Ciraltos](https://www.ciraltos.com/entra-domain-services-and-windows-ad-password-hash-synchronization/) · [Troubleshoot password hash synchronization with Microsoft Entra Connect Sync - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/tshoot-connect-password-hash-synchronization)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],**Case study**  
  
This case study is not timed separately. You may use as much exam time as you want to complete each case. However, this exam might include additional case studies and sections. You must manage your time so that you can complete every question on the exam within the allotted time.  
  
To answer the questions in a case study, you must refer to the information supplied in that case study. Case studies can include exhibits and other resources that provide additional details about the scenario. Each question in this case study is independent of the other questions.  
  
At the end of this case study, a review screen appears. This screen lets you review and change your answers before moving to the next exam section. After you begin a new section, you cannot return to this section.  
  
To begin the case study:  
  
To display the first question in this case study, select the **Next** button. Use the buttons in the left pane to explore the case-study content before answering the questions. Selecting these buttons displays information such as business requirements, the existing environment, and problem statements. If the case study includes an **All Information** tab, the information displayed there is identical to the information on the subsequent tabs. When you are ready to answer a question, select the **Question** button to return to the question.  
  
**Overview**  
  
Northwind Traders is a manufacturing company headquartered in New York City.  
  
**Existing Environment**  
  
**Identity Environment**  
  
The on-premises network includes an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named `northwindtraders.com`.  
  
Northwind Traders has a Microsoft Entra tenant and a Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain. The `northwindtraders.com` domain synchronizes with the Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
**Virtual Machines**  
  
The company has an on-premises Hyper-V virtual machine named VM1 with the following configuration:  
  
- Generation: 1  
- Disk size: 2 TB  
- Disk format: VHDX  
- Disk type: Dynamically expanding  
  
**Cloud Services**  
  
Northwind Traders has a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription. The subscription contains 500 users, all assigned Microsoft 365 E5 licenses.  
  
The company has an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783895710450-dxkoybs2.png)  
  
Both subscriptions are linked to the Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
**Requirements**  
  
**Planned Changes**  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following planned changes:  
  
- Deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool that contains 10 session hosts joined to the Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain.  
- Configure VM1 as the source image for the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and upload the image to Azure.  
- Provide access to a custom app named App1 through the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
**Performance Requirements**  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following performance requirements:  
  
- Each Azure Virtual Desktop session host must support 15 user sessions.  
- Assign each new user session to a single session host until that host reaches its maximum session limit.  
  
**Application Requirements**  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following application requirements:  
  
- Microsoft OneDrive must start when users connect to a RemoteApp session in Azure Virtual Desktop.  
- App1 requires a desktop resolution of 1280 x 1024.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
**Disaster Recovery Requirements**  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following disaster recovery requirements for the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment:  
  
- Minimize outages if an Azure region fails.  
- Minimize the recovery time objective (RTO).  
- Minimize administrative effort during a failover.  
  
**Security Requirements**  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following security requirements:  
  
- When users sign in to the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment by using the Azure Virtual Desktop client, they must authenticate by using only their Microsoft Entra username and password.  
- When users sign in to the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment by using a web browser, they must authenticate by using the Microsoft Authenticator app.  
- All Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts deployed by using the VM1 source image must be onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
- The client version and operating system used to connect to the session hosts must be logged.  
- The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
**Networking Requirements**  
  
The Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts must be able to access resources on the on-premises network.  
  
**User Profile Requirements**  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following user profile requirements:  
  
- Users must be able to access share1 by using their Microsoft Entra account.  
- Azure Virtual Desktop user profiles must be managed by using FSLogix.  
- All user profiles must be stored in share1.  
  
What should you do to ensure that the session hosts satisfy the application requirements for App1?

options.text: Modify the Connection information settings for the host pool.
Assign a scaling plan to the host pool.
Modify the Session behaviour settings for the host pool.
Modify the Display settings for the host pool.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop display settings configure host-pool RDP display properties, including the predefined 1280 × 1024 desktop size. Setting this centrally on the host pool ensures that RemoteApp sessions meet App1’s resolution requirement while minimizing administrative effort.

**Learn more:** [Supported RDP properties - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-properties) · [Set custom Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) properties on a host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/customize-rdp-properties)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool running Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session.  
  
You need to configure automatic scaling for the host pool to meet these requirements:  
  
- Distribute new user sessions among all running session hosts.  
- Automatically start another session host when concurrent user sessions exceed 30 users per host.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: an Azure Automation account and the depth-first load balancing algorithm
an Azure Automation account and the breadth-first load balancing algorithm
an Azure load balancer and the breadth-first load balancing algorithm
an Azure load balancer and the depth-first load balancing algorithm

questions.explanation:
Breadth-first load balancing spreads new user sessions across all available session hosts, which provides an even distribution. Azure Automation can run the Azure Virtual Desktop scaling solution to start session-host VMs as session demand reaches the configured per-host limit. Azure Load Balancer does not provide Azure Virtual Desktop session-host load balancing or this scaling function.

**Learn more:** [Configure Azure Virtual Desktop autoscale scaling plans](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan) · [Set up scaling of session hosts using Azure Automation and Azure Logic Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-scaling-script)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has 10 session hosts deployed by using an Azure Resource Manager (ARM) template.  
  
You find that Windows licenses were **not** applied to the session hosts.  
  
You need to use a PowerShell script to update the licenses.  
  
Which cmdlet should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
The Windows licensing benefit is applied to each underlying Azure virtual machine by setting its `LicenseType` (for example, `Windows_Client`) and updating that VM. `Update-AzVM` persists this VM-level license configuration; Azure Virtual Desktop session-host cmdlets do not set the VM license type.

**Learn more:** [Apply Windows license to session host virtual machines - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/apply-windows-license)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant containing a resource group named RG1. RG1 includes the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783844647135-vwp9pzyc.png)  
  
Your on-premises network uses the IP address range `192.168.10.0/24`. Users on Host1 can successfully connect to the resources on that network.  
  
You add another on-premises network with an IP address range of `192.168.11.0/24` that contains a subnet. The subnet contains an application server named App1.  
  
Users report that Host1 cannot connect to App1.  
  
You need to ensure that users on Host1 can access App1.  
  
What should you modify?

options.text: the DNS server settings of VNet1
the RDP Properties of the host pool

questions.explanation:
A local network gateway defines the on-premises address prefixes that Azure routes through the site-to-site VPN. Add `192.168.11.0/24` to LNGW1’s address space in its Configuration settings so traffic from Host1 to App1 is routed to the new on-premises network.

**Learn more:** [Modify local network gateway settings using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-modify-local-network-gateway-portal) · [Azure VPN Gateway configuration settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-about-vpn-gateway-settings)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create the virtual machines displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783814569250-dyao2vh4.png)  
  
You need a source virtual hard disk for deployments of new Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts. The source operating system must have user-specific and machine-specific information removed.  
  
Which virtual machine can you use as the source?
questions.explanation:
A generalized Windows VM has been prepared with Sysprep, which removes personal account and security information and readies the operating system for reuse as an image. Therefore, only the VM in the generalized state meets the requirement; specialized images retain machine-specific information.

**Learn more:** [Deprovision or generalize a VM before creating an image - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/generalize)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 located in the East US region.  
  
You also have a storage account named storage1 that holds FSLogix profile containers. In the East US region, there is a shared image gallery named SIG1 containing a virtual machine image named Image1. Image1 is used to create new session hosts in Pool1.  
  
You are planning to deploy a new Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool2 in the South India region.  
  
You need to design a session host deployment solution for Pool2 that satisfies the following requirements:  
  
- Image1 must be replicated to the South India region.  
- The session hosts in Pool2 must be created from Image1.  
- Any changes made to Image1 must be available in both the South India and East US regions.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: Create a new shared image gallery named SIG2 in the South India region. Upload a copy of Image1 to SIG2.
Create a new Azure Storage account named storage2 in the South India region. Copy Image1 to a shared folder in storage2.
From SIG1, update the replication for the latest image version of Image1.
Configure geo-redundant storage (GRS) replication for storage1. Copy the VHD file of Image1 to the FSLogix profile container.

questions.explanation:
Azure Compute Gallery (formerly Shared Image Gallery) allows you to specify multiple target replication regions for each image version. By updating the replication settings of the latest version of Image1 in SIG1 to include the South India region, the same image becomes available for deploying session hosts in Pool2 while remaining centrally managed. Since it's the same image (not a copy), any future updates or new versions created in SIG1 will replicate to both East US and South India, satisfying the requirement that changes to Image1 be available in both regions. Creating a separate gallery (SIG2) would break this synchronization, and storage account replication options are unrelated to VM image distribution for AVD session hosts.

**Learn more:** [Store and share images in an Azure Compute Gallery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/shared-image-galleries) · [Create and manage image versions and replication - Azure Compute Gallery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/image-version)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment containing the host pools shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783893999949-4wqegwyy.png)  
  
You need to set up private access for the deployment.  
  
What is the minimum number of private endpoints you should create?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop private access to session-host connections uses a private endpoint for the `connection` subresource of every host pool. Three host pools therefore require three private endpoints; the number of session hosts and their locations do not alter this requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Private Link with Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/private-link-overview)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You deploy and configure Azure Virtual Desktop in a secondary location. You plan to conduct a test failover to that secondary location, but you find existing user sessions in the primary location.  
  
You need to sign users out from the session hosts in the primary location.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
`Remove-AzWvdUserSession` removes a user session from a specified Azure Virtual Desktop session host, thereby signing the user out. It is the current cmdlet in the `Az.DesktopVirtualization` module for this operation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Remove-AzWvdUserSession (Az.DesktopVirtualization)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.desktopvirtualization/remove-azwvdusersession?view=azps-15.5.0)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You deploy and configure Azure Virtual Desktop in a secondary location. You plan to conduct a test failover to that secondary location, but you find existing user sessions in the primary location.  
  
You need to sign users out from the session hosts in the primary location.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
`VHDLocations` specifies the SMB share path where FSLogix Profile Containers locate and create users’ profile VHD/VHDX files. A common setting can be applied across the session hosts, minimizing administration. `CCDLocations` is for Cloud Cache, while the other settings do not define the profile-storage location.

**Learn more:** [Configure profile containers - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-containers) · [FSLogix configuration settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/reference-configuration-settings)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network contains an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain called contoso.com.  
  
You have an Azure subscription linked to a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Contoso.com synchronizes with contoso.onmicrosoft.com.  
  
You have a partner company with a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com.  
  
Contoso.onmicrosoft.com contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879380897-wbjlz32i.png)  
  
You deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has 10 session hosts joined to Contoso.com.  
  
You assign Group1 to the application group in Pool1.  
  
You need to identify the users who will be able to sign in to the session hosts in Pool1.  
  
Which users should you identify?
questions.explanation:
An AD DS-joined Azure Virtual Desktop session host requires a corresponding AD DS user account for the Windows session sign-in. A synchronized hybrid identity satisfies that requirement, so User1 can sign in. Cloud-only identities are supported when session hosts are Microsoft Entra joined, and external identities likewise require Microsoft Entra-joined session hosts with additional configuration; neither condition applies here.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Desktop identities and authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/authentication) · [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites)

questions.question: Which setting must be modified for VNET4 before Pool4 can be deployed?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts that join an Active Directory domain require their virtual network to connect to the relevant domain controllers and DNS servers. Configuring VNET4’s DNS servers to use the appropriate domain-controller DNS enables domain-name resolution during session-host deployment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites) · [Configure virtual networking for Microsoft Entra Domain Services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/domain-services/tutorial-configure-networking)

options.text: From Gallery1, create a new VM application definition.
From Gallery1, create a new VM image definition.
From Template1, capture a generalized virtual machine image.
From Template1, capture a specialized virtual machine image.

questions.explanation:
A generalized Azure Compute Gallery image removes machine- and user-specific information from the source VM, allowing each deployed session host to receive its own computer name and identifiers. A specialized image retains the original VM’s computer name and computer-specific information, including items such as the CMID, which can result in duplicates. Capturing Template1 as a generalized VM image can store the resulting image version in Gallery1.

**Learn more:** [Capture an image of a VM using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/capture-image-portal) · [Create a VM from a specialized image version](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/vm-specialized-image-version)

You have an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783792673748-b58sob9w.png)  
  
Which resources can be backed up by using Azure Backup?
questions.explanation:
Azure Backup can protect Azure virtual machines and Azure Files shares. It does not protect Azure Compute Gallery custom images or a custom image stored as a blob as the resources described here; therefore, the supported resources are the VM and the Azure file share.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Backup?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-overview) · [Support matrix for Azure Files backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/azure-file-share-support-matrix)

questions.question:
You plan to deploy Azure Virtual Desktop.  
  
You are deploying Storage Spaces Direct to a cluster that will store FSLogix profile containers. The cluster will **not** use Cloud Witness.  
  
What is the minimum number of virtual machines needed for the cluster?
questions.explanation:
A two-node Storage Spaces Direct deployment requires a quorum witness. When Cloud Witness is not used, a File Share Witness is required; alongside the two Storage Spaces Direct nodes, this results in a minimum of three virtual machines.\
\
**Learn more:** [Using Storage Spaces Direct in guest virtual machine clusters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/storage-spaces/storage-spaces-direct-in-vm) · [Understand cluster and pool quorum on Azure Local and Windows Server clusters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/storage-spaces/quorum)

options.text: From the CPool1 blade in the Azure portal, create a new volume.
From the Azure portal, create an Azure Backup vault and a backup policy.
From the Volume1 blade in the Azure portal, create a snapshot policy.
From the Azure portal, create a Recovery Services vault and a backup policy.

questions.explanation:
FSLogix profiles are stored in the Azure NetApp Files volume, Volume1. An Azure NetApp Files snapshot policy creates scheduled, point-in-time snapshots of that volume, and individual files can be restored from a snapshot to the active file system. This provides file restoration for the stored profiles.

**Learn more:** [Restore individual files in Azure NetApp Files using single-file snapshot restore](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-netapp-files/snapshots-restore-file-single) · [Manage snapshot policies in Azure NetApp Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-netapp-files/snapshot-policy-manage)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You publish a RemoteApp named AppVersion1. You need AppVersion1 to appear in the Remote Desktop client as Sales Contact Application.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you use?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Desktop RemoteApp is an application resource, and its client-facing display name is configured through the application's friendly name. `Update-AzWvdApplication` updates that application and supports the `-FriendlyName` parameter.\
\
**Learn more:** [Update-AzWvdApplication (Az.DesktopVirtualization)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.desktopvirtualization/update-azwvdapplication?view=azps-15.4.0)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You plan to implement FSLogix profiles for this deployment.  
  
You need to configure NTFS permissions on the file share that will store the FSLogix profiles. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
At which level should you apply permissions for CREATOR OWNER?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix recommends granting CREATOR OWNER Modify permission for subfolders and files only. This gives each user the necessary access to the profile directory and files they create, while withholding unnecessary permissions on the root of the profile share.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure SMB Storage Permissions - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-storage-permissions)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool containing 20 Windows 11 session hosts. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- A Windows client license must be applied to every session host.  
- Administrative effort must be kept to a minimum.  
  
What should you use to deploy the session hosts?
questions.explanation:
Creating an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool and its session-host virtual machines in the Azure portal automatically applies the Azure Virtual Desktop Windows license to the session hosts. This meets the Windows client licensing requirement while avoiding manual license assignment or custom automation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Apply Windows license to session host virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/apply-windows-license)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool named Pool1.  
  
Pool1 includes a session host named Host1 that is joined to Azure AD.  
  
You need to confirm whether a Windows license is assigned to Host1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Azure Active Directory admin center, view the product licenses.
From VM1, run the Get-WindowsDeveloperLicense cmdlet.
From the Azure portal, view the properties of Host1.
From Azure Cloud Shell, run the Get-AzVm cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop licensing for a session-host VM is verified by using `Get-AzVM` and checking the VM's `LicenseType` property. A Windows client license assigned to the session host is displayed as `Windows_Client`; a VM without the applied license has an empty `LicenseType`.\
\
**Learn more:** [Apply Windows license to session host virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/apply-windows-license)

You deploy Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts that are Microsoft Entra joined.  
  
Which users support using FSLogix application rule sets?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix Application Rule Set assignments use traditional Active Directory SIDs and do not support Microsoft Entra cloud-only accounts. A user synchronized from on-premises Active Directory has the required identity; a cloud-only member and a guest do not. Rule-set assignment functionality also requires synchronized users and groups and virtual machines with line-of-sight to a domain controller.

**Learn more:** [FSLogix Apps RuleEditor and Rule Sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-fslogix-apps-rule-editor-rule-sets) · [FSLogix FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/overview-faq)

Number of VMs: 3 -

The session hosts have the following configurations:  
  
- Image used to create the virtual machines: Windows 10 Enterprise  
- Virtual machines domain-joined to: On-premises contoso.com domain  
  
You need to ensure that Microsoft EndPoint Manager can be used to manage security updates on the session hosts.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure the session hosts as hybrid Azure AD-joined
Change Host pool type to Pooled
Change Load balancing algorithm to Depth-first

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune, included in Microsoft Endpoint Manager, manages Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts that are Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined. Session hosts joined to an on-premises AD DS domain require Microsoft Entra hybrid join to be managed by Intune, including for security update management.

**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites) · [Manage the operating system of session hosts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/management)

questions.domain: Plan and implement user environments and apps
questions.explanation:
MSIX app attach is the Azure Virtual Desktop feature designed to deliver applications to session hosts by dynamically attaching them at sign-in rather than installing them locally. It requires applications to be packaged as MSIX app packages, which are stored on a network share and mounted to session hosts as needed, effectively containerizing the app delivery while keeping the session host image unmodified. EXE, MSI, and APPX formats are not supported by this app attach mechanism.

**Learn more:** [What is MSIX app attach - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/what-is-app-attach)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1. Sub1 contains an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The deployment includes the session hosts shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783893291448-nx44lat2.png)  
  
Which session hosts can be protected by using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint supports onboarding of Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session (Host1), Windows Server 2022 (Host2), and Windows Server 2019 (Host3); all three are on the supported operating-system list, and Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts running these OSes are explicitly supported. Therefore all three session hosts can be protected, giving answer D. Server onboarding does require an appropriate server license (for example Defender for Servers), but every listed OS is capability-supported, so no host is excluded.

**Learn more:** [Minimum requirements for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/minimum-requirements)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You need to create a host pool. The solution must ensure that, during periods of low CPU utilization, credits can accumulate and then be used to increase performance above the purchased baseline during periods of high CPU utilization.  
  
Which virtual machine series should you specify when creating the pool?
questions.explanation:
Azure B-series virtual machines use CPU credits. They accumulate credits when CPU usage is below the baseline and consume those credits to burst above the baseline during higher-demand periods.\
\
**Learn more:** [B family VM size series - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/general-purpose/b-family)
