questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that contains an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879361005-u05fvk9m.png)  
  
You need to enable Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access pricing for User1.  
  
At which scope should you enable per-user access pricing?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access pricing is enabled by enrolling the Azure subscription used for the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The subscription enrollment applies to access by users connecting to Azure Virtual Desktop resources; it is not configured on an application group, user, session host, or host pool.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enroll in per-user access pricing for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/enroll-per-user-access-pricing)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: Assign the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal the **Owner** role for Sub1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Assigning the Owner role to the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal at the subscription scope grants it the permissions needed to manage Azure Virtual Desktop resources and session-host power operations. Admin1's Desktop Virtualization Contributor role allows the scaling plan to be assigned to the host pool.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: Assign Admin1 the Owner role for Sub1.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Owner role at subscription scope grants full access to manage every resource in the subscription. That access includes the Azure Virtual Desktop host pool and scaling plan management operations required to associate Scaling1 with Pool1.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: You assign the User Access Administrator role for Sub1 to Admin1.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Desktop Virtualization Contributor role allows management of all Azure Virtual Desktop resources except user or group assignments. Assigning a scaling plan to a host pool is a scaling-plan management operation, so Admin1's existing role at the Sub1 scope provides the required permission. The additional User Access Administrator role is not required but does not prevent the assignment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Built-in Azure RBAC roles for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rbac) · [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: Assign the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal the User Access Administrator role for Sub1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop autoscale requires its service principal to have the Desktop Virtualization Power On Off Contributor role at the subscription scope so it can manage session-host power state. The User Access Administrator role only provides permissions to manage Azure role assignments and does not grant the required autoscale operations.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan)

You have an Azure storage account containing the generalized Windows 10 disk images shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783807424190-dfm95m36.png)  
  
You need to create an image to deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop session host. Which disk should you use?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Desktop master image uploaded to an Azure storage account must be converted to a fixed VHD before an Azure image can be created. The fixed-size VHD is therefore the suitable disk format.\
\
**Learn more:** [Prepare and customize a VHD image for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-customize-master-image) · [Prepare a Windows VHD or VHDX to upload to Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/prepare-for-upload-vhd-image)

questions.question:
You have an Azure storage account containing the generalized Windows 10 disk images shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783807424190-dfm95m36.png)  
  
You need to create an image to deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop session host. Which disk should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can evaluate a user’s network location and use named IP-range locations to allow Azure Virtual Desktop access only from the on-premises network while blocking other locations. This is a centralized identity-based control; Azure Firewall and NSG rules control network traffic, while a user-defined route only directs traffic. [Microsoft Learn: Block access by location](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-block-by-location)

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Learn: Block access by location](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-block-by-location)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to deploy Azure Virtual Desktop session-host virtual machines from a preconfigured master image. The master image will be stored in a shared image gallery.  
  
You create a virtual machine named Image1 to serve as the master image. You install applications and make configuration changes to Image1.  
  
You need to ensure that new session-host virtual machines created from Image1 have unique names and security identifiers.  
  
What should you do on Image1 before adding the image to the shared image gallery?

options.text: At a command prompt, run the set computername command.
At a command prompt, run the sysprep command.
From PowerShell, run the rename-computer cmdlet.
From the lock screen of the Windows device, perform a Windows Autopilot Reset.

questions.explanation:
Sysprep generalizes a Windows VM by removing machine-specific information. A generalized image in Azure Compute Gallery can therefore create session hosts with distinct computer identities and security identifiers.

**Learn more:** [Create an Azure Virtual Desktop golden image](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-golden-image) · [Store and share images in an Azure Compute Gallery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/shared-image-galleries)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to deploy FSLogix profile containers for the Seattle office.  
  
Which storage account should you use?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix profile containers should be placed on an Azure Files share in the same Azure region as the session hosts to minimize profile-load latency, and the account must support identity-based SMB authentication for the domain in use. In this case study the Seattle deployment runs in the West US region, and storage2 is the account located in that region with a supported configuration, so it is the correct choice. The other accounts are in different regions or use configurations unsuitable for FSLogix, which would violate the co-location and performance guidance. This matches the published answer key for the question.

**Learn more:** [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile)

You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop session host named VM1.  
  
You plan to deploy an app named App1 that will process Personally Identifiable Information (PII) data.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 is deployed on a confidential virtual machine. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: On VM1, enable Azure Disk Encryption for the operating system disk. Install App1 on the operating system disk.
Deploy a new virtual machine and install App1.
On VM1, enable File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) and install App1.
On VM1, attach a new data disk and enable BitLocker Drive Encryption (BitLocker). Install App1 on the new disk.

questions.explanation:
Azure confidential VMs provide hardware-enforced isolation and protection for data while it is being processed. A confidential VM must be deployed using the Confidential virtual machine security type; enabling OS or data-disk encryption, BitLocker, or File Integrity Monitoring on an existing VM does not make that VM confidential.

**Learn more:** [About Azure confidential VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/confidential-vm-overview) · [Create an Azure confidential VM in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/quick-create-confidential-vm-portal)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named HostPool1. HostPool1 includes Windows 10 session hosts and the application groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783813603519-f6sd7mk6.jpg)  
  
You need to assign users an instance of a Windows 11 Desktop application group.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Add a session host to HostPool1.

questions.explanation:
A Desktop application group publishes the full desktop from session hosts in its associated host pool. To provide a Windows 11 desktop when HostPool1 contains Windows 10 session hosts, create a separate host pool for Windows 11 session hosts; its Desktop application group can then be assigned to users.

**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites) · [Preferred application group type behavior for pooled host pools in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/preferred-application-group-type)

questions.domain: Plan and implement user environments and apps
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are planning an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that will use existing virtual machines. You have already created an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool.  
  
You need to ensure that you can add the existing virtual machines to the host pool.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
To add existing VMs as session hosts to an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool, you must install the Remote Desktop Agent and Agent Boot Loader on each VM. This installation process requires a host pool registration key (token), which is generated from the host pool and used to associate the VM with that specific host pool during agent setup. Since the host pool already exists, generating this registration key is the necessary first step before the VMs can be registered as session hosts.

**Learn more:** [Add session hosts to a host pool - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/add-session-hosts-host-pool) · [Create a host pool with existing VMs - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/create-host-pool-existing-vm)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You need to ensure users connect to a particular session host every time they sign in. The solution must require minimal administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
A personal host pool maintains a one-to-one mapping between a user and a session host, so each subsequent sign-in is routed to that user's assigned session host. Automatic assignment can assign an available personal desktop at the user's first connection, minimizing administrative work. Pooled-host load balancing does not provide a fixed host assignment, and FSLogix profile containers do not determine session-host routing.

**Learn more:** [Configure personal desktop assignment in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-personal-desktop-assignment-type) · [Configure host pool load balancing in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-load-balancing)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription linked to a Microsoft Entra hybrid tenant named contoso.com. The subscription contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879364239-4m45ow5o.png)  
  
You create a new Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named HP01.  
  
You plan to deploy new session hosts to HP01. The session hosts will connect to VNet01.  
  
You need to ensure that the new session hosts can join contoso.com while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure first?

options.text: the RDP Properties settings of HP01
the default subnet settings of VNet01
the DNS servers settings of VNet01

questions.explanation:
Active Directory domain joining requires the session hosts to resolve the domain and locate its domain controllers through the appropriate DNS servers. Setting custom DNS servers on VNet01 causes newly deployed session hosts to inherit the required DNS configuration, minimizing per-host administration. Azure Virtual Desktop requires the session-host virtual network to connect to the relevant domain controllers and DNS servers when using AD DS.

**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites) · [Troubleshoot Azure Virtual Desktop session host configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-desktop/troubleshoot-vm-configuration)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You need to secure administrative access to the session hosts. The solution must require administrators to use the Azure portal to access the session hosts.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Azure Bastion provides secure RDP or SSH connectivity to virtual machines through the Azure portal while keeping the session hosts reachable through private IP addresses and avoiding exposure of RDP/SSH ports to the public internet.\
\
**Learn more:** [What is Azure Bastion?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/azure/bastion/bastion-overview)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You need to secure administrative access to the session hosts. The solution must require administrators to use the Azure portal to access the session hosts.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

options.text: Install the Remote Desktop Connection Broker role.
Install the Azure Connected Machine agent.
Install the Remote Desktop Services Infrastructure Agent.

questions.explanation:
A custom VM must be registered as a session host by installing the Azure Virtual Desktop Agent, whose installer is the Remote Desktop Services Infrastructure Agent, and supplying a registration token generated for the target host pool. The registration token associates the VM with Pool1.

**Learn more:** [Add session hosts to a host pool - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/add-session-hosts-host-pool)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes an eight-node Storage Spaces Direct cluster named cluster1 and an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. The session hosts in Pool1 store FSLogix user profiles in cluster1.  
  
You are assessing the availability of the user profiles in Pool1.  
  
What is the maximum number of nodes that can fail simultaneously without users losing access to their user profiles?
questions.explanation:
Storage Spaces Direct volumes using three-way mirroring retain three copies of data across separate servers and can remain online and accessible when up to two servers fail at the same time. A third simultaneous server failure can make profile data inaccessible.

**Learn more:** [Storage Spaces Direct overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/storage-spaces/storage-spaces-direct-overview) · [Fault tolerance and storage efficiency on Azure Local and Windows Server clusters](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/storage-spaces/fault-tolerance)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You plan to deploy a host pool named Pool1 that will include 10 session hosts. The session hosts will use MSIX app attach.  
  
Which directory service supports MSIX app attach?

options.text: Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) only
Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) and Microsoft Entra Domain Services only
Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) only
Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Domain Services only
Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Entra Domain Services, and Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS)

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop App Attach supports session hosts joined to either Microsoft Entra ID or an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain. Microsoft Entra Domain Services is not a supported App Attach identity provider.

**Learn more:** [App Attach in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/app-attach-overview) · [Add and manage App Attach applications in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/app-attach-setup)

options.text: Storage Spaces Direct and FSLogix profile containers

questions.explanation:
Azure Files supports SMB-based FSLogix profile containers and uses Azure-managed redundancy options, including geo-redundant storage, to protect data across regions with minimal administrative overhead. Azure NetApp Files can provide cross-region replication, but it requires capacity pools, volumes, and replication configuration; Storage Spaces Direct is self-managed.

**Learn more:** [Business continuity and disaster recovery for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/azure-virtual-desktop/eslz-business-continuity-and-disaster-recovery) · [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure a Group Policy Object (GPO) within the Azure AD DS managed domain.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Domain Services GPOs apply to users and computers in its managed domain. Hybrid-joined desktops belong to the on-premises Active Directory domain, so a GPO in the separate managed domain does not configure their Microsoft Edge security settings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage group policy in Microsoft Entra Domain Services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/domain-services/manage-group-policy) · [Group Policy overview for Windows Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/group-policy/group-policy-overview)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: You configure a Group Policy Object (GPO) within the Azure AD DS managed domain.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Virtual Desktop personal session hosts are hybrid Azure AD joined, which means they remain members of the on-premises Active Directory domain in addition to being registered with Azure AD. Because they are still domain members, they receive Group Policy from on-premises domain controllers in the normal way. Microsoft Edge provides ADMX-based Group Policy templates that let administrators configure browser security settings, and linking a properly configured GPO in the on-premises domain to the organizational unit containing these session hosts will apply those Edge security settings to the personal desktops. This makes the solution valid for meeting the stated requirement.

**Learn more:** [Plan your Microsoft Entra hybrid join deployment - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/devices/hybrid-join-plan) · [Azure Virtual Desktop identities and authentication - Azure Virtual Desktop | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/authentication)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Proposed solution: Configure a compliance policy in Intune.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal of configuring the security settings for the Microsoft Edge browsers on the personal desktops?
questions.explanation:
Intune compliance policies are used to evaluate and report on whether a device meets defined security or configuration criteria (for example, to drive Conditional Access decisions) — they do not push or enforce actual setting values to a device. To configure and enforce Microsoft Edge browser security settings, you need to create a device configuration profile (such as a Settings Catalog or Administrative Templates profile, or apply the Microsoft Edge security baseline) in Intune. Since a compliance policy cannot deliver or enforce Edge settings, this solution does not meet the goal.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Edge policy settings for Windows using Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/configure-edge-with-intune) · [Settings list for the Microsoft Edge security baseline in Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/security-baselines/ref-edge-settings)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Proposed solution: Configure a configuration profile in Intune.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal of configuring the security settings for the Microsoft Edge browsers on the personal desktops?
questions.explanation:
Because the Azure Virtual Desktop personal desktops are already enrolled in Microsoft Intune, an Intune device configuration profile (using Administrative Templates or the Settings Catalog) can be created and assigned to those devices to manage Microsoft Edge policy settings, including security-related settings such as SmartScreen, SSL/TLS controls, extension management, and other browser security policies. Microsoft's official guidance describes configuring Microsoft Edge policy settings for Windows devices through Intune configuration profiles as a supported and recommended method, making this solution valid for the stated requirement.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Edge policy settings for Windows using Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/configure-edge-with-intune) · [Configure Microsoft Edge for Windows with Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/app-management/configuration/configure-edge-windows)

You have an Azure subscription containing a user named User1 and an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. Pool1 includes Microsoft Entra joined session hosts.  
  
User1 has the devices shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879361069-ihja5h4z.png)  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can connect to the session hosts in Pool1 from every device. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the RDP Properties of Pool1, configure the Connection information settings.
From the RDP-Tcp Properties settings of Device3, configure Client Settings.
From Pool1, add a custom RDP property.
From the RDP-Tcp Properties settings of Device1, configure Client Settings.

questions.explanation:
Android clients require the `targetisaadjoined:i:1` custom RDP property to connect to Microsoft Entra joined Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts. Custom RDP properties are configured per host pool, so adding the property to Pool1 enables Device3 without device-specific configuration; the Windows 11 Microsoft Entra-registered and Windows 10 Microsoft Entra-joined devices already meet the Windows client connection requirements.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra joined session hosts in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/azure-ad-joined-session-hosts) · [Set custom RDP properties on a host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/customize-rdp-properties)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment containing a host pool named Pool1. All session hosts in Pool are Microsoft Entra joined.  
  
You have 50 users who will access the deployment from devices running Linux.  
  
You need to ensure that the users can sign in to the deployment.  
  
Which custom RDP property should you configure?
questions.explanation:
The `targetisaadjoined:i:1` custom RDP property permits non-Windows clients, including Linux devices, to connect to Microsoft Entra-joined Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts by entering a username and password.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra joined session hosts in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/azure-ad-joined-session-hosts) · [Supported RDP properties - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-properties)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a session host named Host1.  
  
You need to configure Windows Defender Firewall to permit inbound network traffic for RDP Shortpath on Host1.  
  
Which program in the `C:\Windows\System32` folder should you specify in the inbound firewall rule?
questions.explanation:
The Remote Desktop Services service (TermService), which handles the RDP Shortpath listener and its inbound UDP traffic, runs under `Svchost.exe`. The firewall rule must therefore specify `%SystemRoot%\\System32\\svchost.exe` and associate the rule with the Remote Desktop Services service.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure RDP Shortpath for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-rdp-shortpath)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has these settings:  
  
- Host pool type: Pooled  
- Load balancing algorithm: Breadth-first  
- Max session limit: 5  
- Start VM on connect: Yes  
  
Pool1 includes the session hosts shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879365801-cmocy573.png)  
  
How many more users must connect to Pool1 for Host3 to start?
questions.explanation:
For a pooled host pool, Start VM on Connect waits until the powered-on session hosts reach their maximum session limit before it powers on another session host. Host1 requires 2 more sessions and Host2 requires 3 more sessions to reach the limit of 5, so 5 additional users fill the existing hosts. A sixth user then needs Host3 to be started.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Desktop Start VM on Connect FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/start-virtual-machine-connect-faq) · [Configure Start VM on Connect for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/start-virtual-machine-connect)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription linked to a hybrid Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes the host pools shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879067299-pw229rjn.png)  
  
All session hosts are Microsoft Entra joined.  
  
You plan to deploy FSLogix profile containers and store them on an Azure Files share named `share1`.  
  
Which host pools have session hosts that can access the FSLogix profile containers on `share1`?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Kerberos supports FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files from Microsoft Entra-joined session hosts for hybrid user identities. Windows 10 Enterprise, Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session, Windows Server 2022, and Windows Server 2019 are supported operating systems for these Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts; therefore, all four pools qualify when Azure Files authentication and permissions are configured.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra joined session hosts in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/azure-ad-joined-session-hosts) · [Store FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-container-entra-id-hybrid)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing 500 users. The users have Microsoft Office 365 E1 licenses.  
  
You deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop solution with Windows 10 multi-session hosts and publish a custom remote app named App1.  
  
You need to ensure that the users are licensed to stream App1 while minimizing costs.  
  
Which license should you use?

options.text: a Remote Desktop Services (RDS) client access license (CAL)

questions.explanation:
For Azure Virtual Desktop using Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session hosts, every user needs an eligible license. Windows Enterprise E3 is an eligible per-user license; Office 365 licenses alone do not provide that Windows entitlement. It meets the access requirement without the additional capabilities and cost of Microsoft 365 E5.\
\
**Learn more:** [Licensing Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/licensing)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool.  
  
You need to install Microsoft Antimalware for Azure on the session hosts.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add an extension to each session host.
From a Group Policy Object (GPO), enable Windows 10 security features.
Configure the RDP Properties of the host pool.
Sign in to each session host and install a Windows feature.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Antimalware for Azure is installed and configured through the Microsoft Antimalware VM extension. Because each Azure Virtual Desktop session host is a virtual machine, the extension must be added to every session host.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Antimalware Extension for Windows VMs on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/iaas-antimalware-windows)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool.  
  
You need to install Microsoft Antimalware for Azure on the session hosts.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From RDP Properties for Pool1, configure the Session behavior settings.
On each session host, configure a local Group Policy setting.
To each session host, add an extension.
From RDP Properties for Pool1, configure the Display settings.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop screen capture protection is enabled by the **Enable screen capture protection** policy under the Azure Virtual Desktop administrative template on the computers that provide remote sessions. It is not a host-pool RDP Display or Session behavior setting. In the absence of centralized policy management in the stated environment, the applicable choice is to configure that local Group Policy setting on each session host.

**Learn more:** [Screen capture protection in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/screen-capture-protection)

You plan to enable Start VM on connect for Pool1.  
  
You create a custom Azure role named Role1 that has sufficient permissions to start virtual machines on demand.  
  
You need to ensure that the session hosts in Pool1 can be started on demand.  
  
To which service principal should you assign Role1?
questions.explanation:
Start VM on Connect uses the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal to power on session host virtual machines. Therefore, the custom role that grants VM-start permissions must be assigned to that service principal (at the required subscription scope). [Configure Start VM on Connect for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/start-virtual-machine-connect)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You intend to deploy Azure Virtual Desktop.  
  
You need to maximize network throughput for the session hosts in the deployment.  
  
What has the greatest impact on each session host's network throughput?
questions.explanation:
Azure assigns network bandwidth on a per-VM basis, and the allocated throughput depends on the virtual machine size; larger VM sizes are allocated relatively more bandwidth. Additional network interfaces share that VM-level limit, while Accelerated Networking can help reach the allocated limit but does not increase it. [Virtual machine network bandwidth — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-machine-network-throughput)

**Learn more:** [Virtual machine network bandwidth — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-machine-network-throughput)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You plan to deploy the host pools shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783904082896-mo363urk.png)  
  
For which host pools can you configure a load-balancing algorithm?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop supports the breadth-first and depth-first load-balancing algorithms for pooled host pools. Personal host pools use a user-to-session-host assignment model instead. Therefore, the pooled host pools Pool1 and Pool3 can have a load-balancing algorithm configured.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure host pool load balancing in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-load-balancing)

Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Storage virtual network service endpoint provides a direct route from the virtual network to Azure Storage over the Microsoft Azure backbone network. The regional `Microsoft.Storage` endpoint supports connectivity to storage accounts in the same region as the virtual network.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview) · [Azure Storage firewall rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool named Poo11.  
  
You plan to use a custom image template to create session hosts for Pool1.  
  
You need to create the custom image template.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop custom image templates use Azure Image Builder, which uses a user-assigned managed identity while creating and distributing a custom image. The identity provides the permissions Azure Image Builder needs to create supporting resources and distribute the resulting image.

**Learn more:** [Use custom image templates to create custom images - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/create-custom-image-templates) · [Create an Azure Image Builder Bicep file or ARM template JSON template](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/image-builder-json)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool with these settings:  
  
- Resource group: RG1  
- Host pool name: Pool1  
- Location: East US  
- Host pool type: Pooled  
  
The deployment includes the workspaces shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783811420846-haeu1nbl.jpg)  
  
For Pool1, you plan to create a RemoteApp application group named AppGroup1.  
  
In which workspaces can AppGroup1 be registered?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Desktop workspace and each associated application group must be in the same Azure region. AppGroup1, created for the East US host pool, can therefore be registered with the East US workspaces: Workspace1 and Workspace3. The resource group does not need to match.

**Learn more:** [Move Azure Virtual Desktop resources between regions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/move-resources)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. Pool1 includes session hosts running Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session.  
  
You need to use Performance Monitor to troubleshoot a poor frame-quality issue affecting a current user session in Pool1.  
  
Which performance counter should you use?
questions.explanation:
Poor frame quality in an Azure Virtual Desktop remote session is diagnosed with the **Frame Quality** counter under **RemoteFX Graphics** in Performance Monitor. It reports output-frame quality as a percentage of source-frame quality for the session.\
\
**Learn more:** [Diagnose graphics performance issues in Remote Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/remotefx-graphics-performance-counters)

You have an Azure subscription containing a Windows Server virtual machine named Server1, deployed in the West US Azure region.  
  
You deploy a new Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named HostPool1 in the East US Azure region.  
  
You need to ensure all traffic between HostPool1 and Server1 is routed through the Microsoft backbone network.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Virtual network peering, including global virtual network peering across regions, provides private connectivity between Azure virtual networks. Traffic between peered virtual networks remains on the Microsoft backbone network rather than traversing the public internet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network peering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-peering-overview)

questions.explanation:
For Azure Virtual Desktop SSO, enabling Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP requires setting `isRemoteDesktopProtocolEnabled` to `true` on the `remoteDesktopSecurityConfiguration` object of the **Windows Cloud Login** service principal. This enables issuance of RDP access tokens for sign-in to Microsoft Entra joined Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts.

**Learn more:** [Configure single sign-on for Azure Virtual Desktop using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-single-sign-on?WT.mc_id=Portal-Microsoft_Azure_WVD) · [remoteDesktopSecurityConfiguration resource type](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/remotedesktopsecurityconfiguration?view=graph-rest-1.0)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. Pool1 is deployed in the US East Azure region and has 10 session hosts.  
  
You need to deploy session hosts in the West Europe Azure region and join those session hosts to Pool1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Replicate the session host virtual machines to the West Europe region.
Generate a new registration key for Pool1.
In the West Europe region, create a network security group (NSG).

questions.explanation:
A host-pool registration key authorizes Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts to join the host pool. Session hosts may be deployed in a different Azure region from the host pool, so cross-region replication, virtual-network peering, and a new network security group are not inherent prerequisites. Microsoft’s procedure for adding session hosts begins by generating a registration key for the target host pool.

**Learn more:** [Add session hosts to a host pool - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/add-session-hosts-host-pool) · [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 that contains two session hosts named Host1 and Host2. The session hosts use FSLogix user profiles.  
  
Host1 has the local groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783885620262-u4bfbee2.png)  
  
Host2 has the local groups shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783885625484-4e7sxdgb.png)  
  
User1 connects to Pool and changes their desktop.  
  
User1 reports that, when reconnecting to Pool, the desktop changes do not appear.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 sees the modified desktop when connecting to Pool. The solution must minimize the impact on other user profiles.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add User1 to both FSLogix Profile Include list groups.
Remove Group2 from both FSLogix Profile Exclude list groups.

questions.explanation:
FSLogix profile include groups allow eligible users to be processed, but membership in an FSLogix profile exclude group prevents the profile container from being used. User1 is included through Group1 but is also indirectly excluded through Group3's membership in Group2. Removing User1 from Group3 removes only User1's exclusion, allowing the FSLogix profile to persist desktop changes while retaining the exclusion for other users.

**Learn more:** [Local include and exclude groups - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-include-exclude-groups) · [FSLogix Codes and what they mean](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/troubleshooting-error-codes)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool named Pool1.  
  
You plan to create a Windows 10 image named Image1 for deploying new session hosts to Pool1.  
  
You need to ensure that every new session host deployed by using Image1 is onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Run a Defender for Endpoint onboarding script on Image1, and then run sysprep.
Add a Defender for Endpoint onboarding script to image1, and then run the script at first start.
Create an MSIX package for Pool1.
Create an automation task for Pool1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft recommends adding the Defender for Endpoint onboarding script to the Azure Virtual Desktop golden image and configuring it as a startup script so that it runs at first boot on every session host provisioned from that image. The golden image itself should not be onboarded, because cloned hosts can otherwise inherit the same Defender for Endpoint registration identity.

**Learn more:** [Onboard Windows devices in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/onboard-windows-multi-session-device) · [Onboard non-persistent virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) devices in Microsoft Defender](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-endpoints-vdi)

You need to make sure users connecting to Azure Virtual Desktop sessions must reauthenticate every six hours.

Microsoft Entra Conditional Access provides the sign-in frequency session control used to require periodic reauthentication for Azure Virtual Desktop. A Conditional Access policy must be created before configuring its sign-in frequency to six hours.\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com and an Azure virtual network named VNET1.  
  
You deploy an Azure Active Directory Domain Services (Azure AD DS) managed domain named litwareinc.com to VNET1.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 to VNET1.  
  
You need to ensure that Windows 10 Enterprise session hosts can be deployed to Pool1.

Modify the DNS settings of VNET1.
Add a custom domain name to contoso.com.
Implement Azure AD Connect cloud sync.

The virtual network must therefore be configured to use the Azure AD DS managed domain controllers as its DNS servers, allowing the session hosts to resolve the domain and locate its domain controllers.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to recommend an authentication solution that satisfies the performance requirements.  
  
Which two actions should be included in the recommendation? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Join all the session hosts to Azure AD.
In each Azure region that will contain the Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, create an Azure Active Directory Domain Service (Azure AD DS) managed domain.
Deploy domain controllers for the on-premises Active Directory domain on Azure virtual machines to the new sites..
Deploy read-only domain controllers (RODCs) on Azure virtual machines to the new sites.
In each Azure region that will contain the Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, create an Active Directory site.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts that use Active Directory Domain Services must be able to connect to domain controllers and relevant DNS servers. Deploying replica domain controllers for the existing on-premises AD DS domain in the new Azure sites supplies local directory and Kerberos authentication services. Creating an Active Directory site for each Azure region associates its subnets with that site so clients locate local domain controllers and Active Directory can manage intersite replication appropriately.

**Learn more:** [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites) · [Install Active Directory Domain Services on an Azure virtual machine](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/deploy/virtual-dc/adds-on-azure-vm)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool. The pool contains session hosts running Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session.  
  
You connect to a Remote Desktop session on Pool1 and notice a problem with how often the screen updates.  
  
You need to determine whether this issue is caused by insufficient server, network, or client resources, and the solution must minimize the time it takes to identify which resource type is responsible.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From within the current session, use the Azure Virtual Desktop Experience Estimator.
From Azure Cloud Shell, run the Get-AzOperationalInsightsWorkspaceUsage cmdlet and specify the DefaultProfile parameter.
From Azure Cloud Shell, run the Get-AzWvdUserSession cmdlet and specify the UserSessionId parameter.
From within the current session, use Performance Monitor to display the values of all the RemoteFX Graphics(*)\Frames Skipped/Second counters.

questions.explanation:
Performance Monitor exposes the RemoteFX Graphics(*) performance object, which includes separate 'Frames Skipped/Second' counters for Insufficient Server Resources, Insufficient Client Resources, and Insufficient Network Resources. Viewing all three counters together within the active session lets you immediately see which resource category is causing frames to be skipped, providing the fastest way to pinpoint the bottleneck type. This is documented by Microsoft under 'Diagnose graphics performance issues in Remote Desktop' for Azure Virtual Desktop.

**Learn more:** [Diagnose graphics performance issues Remote Desktop - Azure - Azure Virtual Desktop | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/remotefx-graphics-performance-counters)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.explanation:
The Desktop Virtualization Application Group Contributor role grants full management rights over an application group (such as adding/removing applications and editing group properties) but deliberately excludes the ability to assign users or groups to it, in line with Azure Virtual Desktop's least-privilege RBAC design. Assigning users or groups to a resource (creating a role assignment such as 'Desktop Virtualization User' on the application group) requires the User Access Administrator role, since that is the built-in role that grants permission to manage access assignments. Combining these two built-in roles lets Admin1 both administer the application group and assign users to it, without granting excessive rights over host pools or workspaces.

**Learn more:** [Built-in Azure RBAC roles Azure Virtual Desktop - Azure Virtual Desktop | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rbac) · [Azure built-in roles - Azure RBAC | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and implement FSLogix profile containers.  
  
You need to ensure that specific users do not use the FSLogix profile containers.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Modify the local groups on each session host
Apply an Application Masking rule to each session host
Apply an AppLocker policy to each session host
Modify the RDP Properties of the host pool

questions.explanation:
FSLogix provides local include and exclude groups for each container type. Adding users to the profile-container exclude group prevents the FSLogix service from processing them, so their FSLogix profile containers are not used.\
\
**Learn more:** [Local include and exclude groups - FSLogix | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-include-exclude-groups)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and implement FSLogix profile containers.  
  
You need to ensure that specific users do not use the FSLogix profile containers.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure identity for all the session hosts.
In each Azure region that will contain the Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, create an Azure Active Directory Domain Service (Azure AD DS) managed domain.
Deploy domain controllers for the on-premises Active Directory domain on Azure virtual machines to the new sites.
Deploy read-only domain controllers (RODCs) on Azure virtual machines to the new sites.
In each Azure region that will contain the Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, create an Active Directory site.

questions.explanation:
Because Kerberos authentication for AVD session hosts requires direct network line-of-sight to a domain controller, placing writable domain controllers for the existing on-premises Active Directory domain on Azure virtual machines in each new region ensures that authentication requests are serviced locally instead of crossing a WAN link, which reduces authentication latency. Additionally, defining an Active Directory site for each Azure region that hosts session hosts allows Active Directory Domain Services to correctly map clients to the nearest local domain controller (via the DC Locator/site-aware logic), further ensuring low-latency, local authentication rather than clients being routed to a distant site's domain controller. RODCs are unsuitable because they still depend on writable domain controllers to validate new/uncached credentials, and Azure AD DS would create a separate managed domain rather than extending the existing on-premises identity infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Desktop identities and authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/authentication) · [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites)

You need to ensure that users can connect to a session host while it is deallocated.  
  
On which resources can Start VM on Connect be enabled?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop configures Start VM on Connect per host pool. When a user connects, the service can start a deallocated session-host VM in that host pool. Pool1 is the host pool; the workspace and individual session hosts are not the configuration scope for this feature.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Start VM on Connect for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/start-virtual-machine-connect)

You need to ensure that users can connect to a session host while it is deallocated.  
  
On which resources can Start VM on Connect be enabled?
questions.explanation:
The Remote Desktop client (Windows Desktop client) for Azure Virtual Desktop supports Windows 11, Windows 10 editions, Windows 10 IoT Enterprise, and Windows Server 2012 R2 or later, but it does not support Windows 8 or Windows 8.1. Device1 (Windows 10 Home) and Device3 (Windows 10 IoT Enterprise) meet the supported OS requirements, while Device2 (Windows 8.1 Professional) does not, since Windows 8.1 is explicitly excluded from client support.

Your network contains an on-premises Active Directory domain that synchronizes with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant. The domain includes the domain controllers shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783807962802-acod9xhq.png)  
  
The DNS servers are configured to forward requests to an external DNS service.  
  
You create a new virtual network named VNET2, which is peered with VNET1 and has gateway transit enabled.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool in VNET2. The session hosts will join the Active Directory domain.  
  
You need to configure DNS to meet the following requirements:  
  
- Ensure that Azure Virtual Desktop users can resolve on-premises servers and Azure resources.  
- Ensure that Azure Virtual Desktop remains operational if a DNS server fails.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: the DNS settings of VNET2 to use Server2 and Server1
the DNS settings of VNET2 to use the Azure DNS service
the DNS settings of the virtual machines to use Server2 and Server1
the DNS settings of the virtual machines to use the Azure DNS service

questions.explanation:
Custom DNS is required so the domain-joined session hosts can resolve the on-premises Active Directory namespace. Configuring VNET2 to use Server2 and Server1 applies the DNS configuration network-wide to the session hosts, rather than requiring configuration on each virtual machine. The DNS servers can resolve domain names and forward other queries to the external DNS service, while listing both servers provides resilience if either DNS server fails. Microsoft recommends network-wide DNS settings where possible and identifies customer-managed DNS servers as a solution for resolving on-premises names from Azure virtual machines.

**Learn more:** [Configure DNS name resolution for Azure virtual networks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-networks-name-resolution-for-vms-and-role-instances) · [Azure Virtual Network FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-networks-faq)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory Domain Services (Azure AD DS) managed domain called contoso.com.  
  
You create an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 and assign the Virtual Machine Contributor role on the Azure subscription to a user named Admin1.  
  
You need to ensure that Admin1 can add session hosts to Pool1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Assign Admin1 the Desktop Virtualization Host Pool Contributor role for Pool1
Assign Admin1 the Desktop Virtualization Session Host Operator role for Pool1
Add Admin1 to the AAD DC Administrators group
Assign a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 license to Admin1

questions.explanation:
Creating and adding Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts requires both Virtual Machine Contributor and Desktop Virtualization Host Pool Contributor permissions. Admin1 already has the VM permission, so assign Desktop Virtualization Host Pool Contributor only on Pool1. Session hosts joined to an Azure AD DS managed domain require an account with permission to join computers to that domain; members of the AAD DC Administrators group have that permission.

**Learn more:** [Add session hosts to a host pool - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/add-session-hosts-host-pool) · [Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an on-premises Active Directory domain named contoso.com that synchronizes with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 with the following settings:  
  
* Host pool name: Pool1  
* Host pool type: Personal  
* Number of VMs: 3  
  
The session hosts have the following configurations:  
  
* Image used to create the virtual machines: Windows 10 Enterprise8  
* Virtual machines domain-joined to: On-premises contoso.com domain  
  
You need to ensure that Microsoft EndPoint Manager can be used to manage security updates on the session hosts.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Change Host pool type to Pooled and specify Load balancing algorithm as Depth-first.
Change Host pool type to Pooled and specify Load balancing algorithm as Breadth-first.
Configure the session hosts as hybrid Azure AD-joined.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Intune can manage Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts that are Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined. For session hosts joined to an on-premises AD DS domain, Microsoft Entra Connect must enable Microsoft Entra hybrid join before they can be managed through Intune.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Desktop prerequisites — Session host management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/prerequisites) · [Manage the operating system of session hosts — Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/management)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool called Pool1.  
  
You are troubleshooting an issue in which a Remote Desktop client has stopped responding.  
  
You need to restore the Remote Desktop client’s default settings and unsubscribe from every workspace.  
  
Which command should you run?
questions.explanation:
The Remote Desktop client executable `msrdcw.exe` supports the `/reset` option to reset user data. Resetting this data restores the client’s default settings and unsubscribes it from all workspaces.\
\
**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot the Remote Desktop client for Windows when connecting to Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/remote-desktop-client/troubleshoot-client-windows)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 that runs Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session hosts.  
  
You need to use Performance Monitor to troubleshoot a low frame-quality issue affecting a current user session in Pool1.  
  
What should you run to obtain the user session ID?
questions.explanation:
`qwinsta` displays Remote Desktop Session Host session information, including the ID for each active session. That ID can be used to identify the affected user session when collecting or examining session-specific Performance Monitor data.\
\
**Learn more:** [qwinsta | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/qwinsta)

options.text: Select Exclude from latest for image version 1.0.0.
Select Exclude from latest for image version 1.2.0.
Apply a lock to image version 1.1.0.
Apply a tag named default to image version 1.1.0.

questions.explanation:
Azure Compute Gallery selects the highest eligible image version when a deployment uses the image definition's latest version. Excluding version 1.2.0 from latest removes the higher version from consideration, so version 1.1.0 becomes the default eligible version. The `excludeFromLatest` setting is specifically defined to prevent virtual machines deployed from the latest image-definition version from using that image version.

**Learn more:** [Gallery Image Versions - Create Or Update - REST API (Azure Compute)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/compute/gallery-image-versions/create-or-update?view=rest-compute-2025-04-01) · [Overview of Azure Compute Gallery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/azure-compute-gallery)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool containing 20 Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session hosts.  
  
Users access the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment from computers running Windows 10.  
  
You plan to implement FSLogix Application Masking.  
  
You need to deploy Application Masking rule sets while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
Where should you copy the rule sets?

options.text: the FSLogix profile container of each user
C:\Program Files\FSLogix\Apps\Rules on every Windows 10 computer
C:\Program Files\FSLogix\Apps\Rules on every session host

questions.explanation:
FSLogix Application Masking rule and assignment files are deployed to each virtual machine on which they must take effect, in `C:\Program Files\FSLogix\Apps\Rules`. The Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts run the user sessions and the FSLogix Apps service, so the rule sets belong in that directory on every session host.

**Learn more:** [Create and Implement Rule Sets (Application Masking)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/tutorial-application-rule-sets)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You plan to create the host pools shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783879060904-9uzxt7hx.png)  
  
You plan to grant external users access to the session hosts.  
  
You need to ensure that Azure Virtual Desktop connections are licensed by using per-user access pricing.  
  
To which host pools will per-user access pricing apply?
questions.explanation:
For external commercial use, Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access pricing supports Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session and Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session. It is not supported for Windows Server session hosts, including Windows Server 2016 and Windows Server 2022 Datacenter: Azure Edition.

**Learn more:** [Licensing Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/licensing)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 that has three session hosts. The session hosts are configured to use FSLogix profile containers.  
  
You need to configure Cloud Cache on the session hosts.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a VHDLocations entries to the Windows registry
Remove VHDLocations entries from the Windows registry

questions.explanation:
FSLogix Cloud Cache uses the `CCDLocations` setting rather than `VHDLocations`. `VHDLocations` and `CCDLocations` must not both be configured, so the existing `VHDLocations` registry entries must be removed when changing profile containers to Cloud Cache.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Configure Profile Containers with Cloud Cache - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/tutorial-cloud-cache-containers) · [Configuration Settings - FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/reference-configuration-settings)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a main office and two branch offices, each of which connects directly to the internet. The router in each branch office is configured as an endpoint for the following VPNs:  
  
- A VPN connection to the main office  
- A site-to-site VPN to Azure  
  
The routers in each branch office have the Quality of Service (QoS) rules shown in the exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784171679856-5uhvbft8.png)  
  
Users in the branch offices report slow responses and connection errors when they attempt to connect to Azure Virtual Desktop resources.  
  
You need to modify the QoS rules on the branch office routers to improve Azure Virtual Desktop performance.  
  
For which rule should you increase the bandwidth allocation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop client and session connectivity (including RDP Shortpath and the AVD service/control-plane traffic) occurs over HTTPS (TCP 443) directly to Azure and Microsoft 365 public IP address ranges, not through the site-to-site VPN tunnel. Therefore, the rule governing HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Azure and Microsoft 365 public IP addresses (Rule3) is the one that needs more bandwidth allocated to resolve the slow response and connection errors experienced when connecting to Azure Virtual Desktop.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Azure Virtual Desktop network connectivity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/network-connectivity) · [RDP Shortpath for managed networks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-shortpath)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment with five session hosts.  
  
Users work from offices in Seattle and Vancouver and connect to the session hosts over the internet.  
  
You need to ensure that users can connect to the session hosts only from the Seattle and Vancouver offices.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can evaluate a user's public IP-based network location through named locations. Defining the Seattle and Vancouver office egress IP ranges as named locations and applying a Conditional Access policy to Azure Virtual Desktop restricts connections to those offices. Azure Virtual Desktop uses reverse-connect transport by default, so inbound network rules on the session hosts do not control the normal client connection path.

**Learn more:** [Conditional Access Policy: Using Network Signals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-assignment-network) · [Understanding Azure Virtual Desktop network connectivity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/network-connectivity)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The session hosts are joined to an on-premises Active Directory domain named contoso.com. You need to limit user sessions to three hours. What should you configure?

options.text: a Group Policy Object (GPO) in contoso.com.
the RDP Properties of a host pool

questions.explanation:
A Group Policy Object linked to the organizational unit containing the domain-joined session hosts can configure Remote Desktop Session Host session time limits, including a three-hour limit for active sessions. Workspace properties and host-pool RDP properties do not enforce Windows session-duration limits; JIT VM access governs administrative VM access.

**Learn more:** [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan) · [Troubleshoot Autoscale Issues in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-desktop/troubleshoot-autoscale)

You create a Recovery Services vault named Vault1.  
  
Which resources can you back up to Vault1 by using Azure Backup?
questions.explanation:
Azure Backup in a Recovery Services vault supports Azure virtual machines and Azure file shares. It does not back up Shared Image Gallery images or custom VM images stored as Azure Blob storage objects as Azure VM backup items. Therefore, the supported resources are AVDVM-0 and share1.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Backup?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-overview) · [Azure Backup architecture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-architecture)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Case study —  
  
This case study is not timed separately. You may use as much of the exam time as needed to complete each case. However, this exam might include additional case studies and sections. You must manage your time so that you can complete every question on the exam within the allotted time.  
  
To answer the questions in a case study, you must refer to the information provided in that case study. Case studies can include exhibits and other resources that provide additional details about the scenario described. Each question in this case study is independent of the others.  
  
At the end of this case study, a review screen will appear. This screen lets you review and change your answers before moving to the next exam section. After you start a new section, you cannot return to this section.  
  
To begin the case study —  
  
To show the first question in this case study, select the **Next** button. Use the buttons in the left pane to review the case-study content before answering the questions. Selecting these buttons displays information such as business requirements, the existing environment, and problem statements. If the case study includes an **All Information** tab, the information shown there is identical to that shown on the later tabs. When you are ready to answer a question, select the **Question** button to return to it.  
  
Overview —  
  
Northwind Traders is a manufacturing company headquartered in New York City.  
  
Existing Environment —  
  
Identity Environment —  
  
The on-premises network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named `northwindtraders.com`.  
  
Northwind Traders has a Microsoft Entra tenant and a Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain. The `northwindtraders.com` domain synchronizes with the Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
Virtual Machines —  
  
The company has an on-premises Hyper-V virtual machine named VM1 with the following configuration:  
  
- Generation: 1  
- Disk size: 2 TB  
- Disk format: VHDX  
- Disk type: Dynamically expanding  
  
Cloud Services —  
  
Northwind Traders has a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription. The subscription contains 500 users, each assigned a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  
  
The company also has an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783893140365-mf99g75x.png)  
  
Both subscriptions are linked to the Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
Requirements —  
  
Planned Changes —  
  
Northwind Traders identifies these planned changes:  
  
- Deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool containing 10 session hosts joined to the Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain.  
- Configure VM1 as the source image for the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and upload the image to Azure.  
- Provide access to a custom app named App1 through the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
Performance Requirements —  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following performance requirements:  
  
- Every Azure Virtual Desktop session host must support 15 user sessions.  
- Each new user session must be assigned to one session host until that host reaches its maximum session limit.  
  
Application Requirements —  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following application requirements:  
  
- Microsoft OneDrive must open when users connect to an Azure Virtual Desktop RemoteApp session.  
- App1 requires a desktop resolution of 1280 x 1024.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
Disaster Recovery Requirements —  
  
Northwind Traders identifies these disaster recovery requirements for the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment:  
  
- Minimize outages when an Azure region fails.  
- Minimize the recovery time objective (RTO).  
- Minimize administrative effort during a failover.  
  
Security Requirements —  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following security requirements:  
  
- When users sign in to the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment by using the Azure Virtual Desktop client, they must authenticate using only their Microsoft Entra username and password.  
- When users sign in to the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment by using a web browser, they must authenticate by using the Microsoft Authenticator app.  
- Every Azure Virtual Desktop session host deployed by using the VM1 source image must be onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
- The client version and operating system used to connect to the session hosts must be logged.  
- The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Networking Requirements —  
  
The Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts must be able to access resources on the on-premises network.  
  
User Profile Requirements —  
  
Northwind Traders identifies the following user profile requirements:  
  
- Users must be able to access share1 by using their Microsoft Entra account.  
- Azure Virtual Desktop user profiles must be managed by using FSLogix.  
- All user profiles must be stored in share1.  
  
Which two actions should you take to meet the Defender for Endpoint security requirements? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Add a Defender for Endpoint onboarding script to VM1 and run the script at first startup.
Use a Group Policy Object (GPO) to run an on boarding script from a shared location.
Create an app attach image for the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.
Run a Defender for Endpoint onboarding script on VM1 before generalizing the VM1 source image.

questions.explanation:
For Azure Virtual Desktop hosts provisioned from a golden image, Microsoft recommends configuring the Defender for Endpoint VDI onboarding script to run at first startup from the golden image. A centrally stored onboarding script can also be run through a domain Group Policy Object. The golden image itself should not be onboarded before generalization, because the onboarding script must run on the provisioned session hosts.

**Learn more:** [Onboard Windows devices in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/onboard-windows-multi-session-device) · [Onboard non-persistent virtual desktop infrastructure devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-endpoints-vdi)

You have an Azure subscription that contains 10 Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts running Windows 10 Enterprise.  
  
You plan to deploy the new Microsoft Teams app to those session hosts.  
  
You need to prepare the session hosts for deployment.  
  
Which two components should you install? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the Remote Desktop WebRTC Redirector Service

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams media optimization on Azure Virtual Desktop requires the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable on Windows session hosts. The Remote Desktop WebRTC Redirector Service must also be installed on each session host to provide Teams media redirection and optimization.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/teams-on-avd)

options.text: Modify the membership of the FSLogix ODFC Exclude List group.
Modify the membership of the FSLogix Profile Exclude List group.

questions.explanation:
FSLogix automatically creates local groups named "FSLogix Profile Exclude List" and "FSLogix ODFC Exclude List" on session hosts. Adding an account to the FSLogix Profile Exclude List group excludes that account from having its profile managed by FSLogix Profile Containers, which is the appropriate way to meet a requirement that a specific admin account (Admin1) not use FSLogix profile management, without having to manually edit registry settings.

**Learn more:** [Configure FSLogix Profile Container - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/tutorial-configure-profile-container)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment containing the host pools shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783878883376-lsj1ymv7.png)  
  
You plan to use app attach.  
  
In which host pools can the session hosts use app attach?
questions.explanation:
App Attach requires session hosts to run a supported Windows client operating system, and Windows Server is not supported. Windows 11 Enterprise and Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session meet that requirement; Windows 10 Pro and Windows Server 2022 Datacenter do not. A host pool’s personal or pooled type and its validation-environment setting do not alter that eligibility.

**Learn more:** [Add and manage App Attach applications in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/app-attach-setup) · [App Attach in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/app-attach-overview)
