questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a RemoteApp named App1.  
  
You discover that from the Save As dialog box of App1, users are able to launch executable applications other than App1 on the session hosts.  
  
You need to ensure that users can run only published applications on the session hosts.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure a conditional access policy in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).
Modify the Access control (IAM) settings of the host pool.
Modify the RDP Properties of the host pool.
Configure an AppLocker policy on the session hosts.

questions.explanation:
The Save As/Open dialog exposed by a RemoteApp can be used to browse the session host file system and launch arbitrary executables, bypassing the intended RemoteApp restriction. Microsoft's recommended solution to lock down which applications users can execute on the session hosts is to configure an AppLocker policy on those session hosts, which enforces rules restricting execution to only the approved/published applications, blocking attempts to run other executables discovered through dialogs like Save As.

**Learn more:** [Restrict what users can do in RemoteApp - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/security-guide#application-security) · [AppLocker overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/windows-defender-application-control/applocker/applocker-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You need to give external users access to the deployment. The external users use computers running Windows 10 Pro and Windows 10 Enterprise, and they cannot install applications.  
  
What should you recommend that the users use to connect to the deployment?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Edge can provide browser-based access to Azure Virtual Desktop without requiring users to install a client application, which meets the restriction against installing applications. The other client-based options require a locally installed application or are not the appropriate browser access method. Microsoft now documents that the legacy Remote Desktop web client is unsupported for public-cloud environments, making this a legacy certification-exam scenario.

**Learn more:** [Use the Remote Desktop client to connect to Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/remote-desktop-client/connect-windows-cloud-services) · [What is Azure Virtual Desktop?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/overview)

You create an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment with these settings:  
  
- Host pool name: Pool1  
- Location: West US  
- Host pool type: Personal  
  
Which images can you use for the session hosts?
questions.explanation:
Session hosts are deployed in West US, so the gallery image version must be replicated and available in West US. A personal Azure Virtual Desktop host pool can use either a generalized or specialized Windows image. Image1 and Image2 meet the regional requirement; the West Europe images do not.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing the storage accounts shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783885389419-dd9cqdev.png)  
  
You deploy Azure Virtual Desktop. All session hosts in the deployment are joined to Active Directory.  
  
You need to implement FSLogix profile containers.  
  
Which storage accounts can be used to store the profile containers?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix profile containers are stored on SMB file shares. Azure Files supports standard file shares in general-purpose v2 storage accounts and premium file shares in FileStorage accounts. Therefore, the standard account (storage1) and the premium FileStorage account (storage4) can host the containers; premium page-blob and block-blob accounts cannot.

**Learn more:** [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile) · [Store FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files and Active Directory Domain Services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-container-azure-files-active-directory)

You must deploy the session hosts to satisfy the deployment requirements.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run **first**?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts must use a registration key to register with their host pool. `New-AzWvdRegistrationInfo` creates the host pool registration information and token needed before the hosts can complete registration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add session hosts to a host pool — Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/add-session-hosts-host-pool) · [New-AzWvdRegistrationInfo — Az.DesktopVirtualization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.desktopvirtualization/new-azwvdregistrationinfo?view=azps-14.6.0)

questions.question:
You must deploy the session hosts to satisfy the deployment requirements.  
  
Which PowerShell cmdlet should you run **first**?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix `VHDLocations` requires an SMB share UNC path. An Azure Files share uses the `\\<storage-account>.file.core.windows.net\<share-name>` format, so the required path is `\\store1.file.core.windows.net\profiles`.

**Learn more:** [Store FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files and AD DS or Microsoft Entra Domain Services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-container-azure-files-active-directory) · [Configure profile containers using FSLogix](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/how-to-configure-profile-containers)

questions.question: Which role must be assigned to Operator2 in order to satisfy the technical requirements?
questions.explanation:
The Desktop Virtualization User Session Operator role provides Azure Virtual Desktop permissions to manage user sessions, such as sending messages, disconnecting users, and signing users out, without broader configuration permissions.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has 60,000 users.  
  
You plan to deploy Azure Virtual Desktop.  
  
You need to recommend a storage solution for FSLogix profile containers. The solution must deliver the highest possible IOPS and the lowest-latency desktop experience.  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Azure NetApp Files provides enterprise-scale SMB storage for FSLogix profile containers and has the highest documented performance of the listed applicable options: up to 460,000 IOPS per volume at approximately 1 ms latency. This makes it suitable for a very large Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that prioritizes maximum IOPS and minimum desktop latency.

**Learn more:** [Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/store-fslogix-profile) · [Storage considerations for Azure Virtual Desktop workloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/azure-virtual-desktop/storage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Which two roles should you assign to Admin2 to satisfy the security requirements? Each correct answer represents part of the complete solution.  
  
(Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
The built-in Desktop Virtualization Application Group Contributor role lets an administrator fully manage application groups but does not include permission to assign users or groups to those application groups, since it lacks the roleAssignments/write action. To allow Admin2 to assign users to the application groups, the User Access Administrator role must also be granted, as it includes the ability to manage role assignments. Together, these two roles let Admin2 manage application groups and assign users to them while following the principle of least privilege, per Microsoft's built-in RBAC roles for Azure Virtual Desktop.

**Learn more:** [Built-in Azure RBAC roles Azure Virtual Desktop - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rbac) · [Delegated access in Azure Virtual Desktop - Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/delegated-access-virtual-desktop)

Pool1 has two session hosts.  
  
You create a new virtual machine named Host3 that runs Windows 11.  
  
You need to add Host3 as the third session host in Pool1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Assign a scaling plan to Pool1.

questions.explanation: An Azure Virtual Desktop session host must be registered to its host pool by using a valid host pool registration key (registration token). Generate that key before configuring Host3 to join Pool1.

Pool1 has two session hosts.  
  
You create a new virtual machine named Host3 that runs Windows 11.  
  
You need to add Host3 as the third session host in Pool1.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
For Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts that are Microsoft Entra joined, connections from macOS and other non-Windows clients require the custom RDP property `targetisaadjoined:i:1`. It enables authentication to the Entra-joined session host by using Microsoft Entra username and password credentials.

You plan to create a new host pool named Pool1 that will include five Windows 11 session hosts.  
  
You need to enable Secure Boot and vTPM on the session hosts.

You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 and a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
The tenant has user accounts for all internal users and for users from a partner company named Fabrikam, Inc. Every internal user has a Microsoft 365 E5 license assigned. Fabrikam users have no licenses assigned.  
  
Sub1 includes an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment with a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 includes a RemoteApp named App1.  
  
You need to configure access to App1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Fabrikam users must be licensed by using Per-user access pricing.  
- App1 must be accessible to every internal and Fabrikam user.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Add the Fabrikam users to the application group that contains App1.
Add a new host pool to Sub1.
Assign a Microsoft 365 F3 license to each Fabrikam user.
Add a new host pool to a new subscription.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop per-user access pricing covers external users accessing published RemoteApps, but an enrolled subscription also incurs access charges for users who already have separate eligible licenses. Internal users already licensed with Microsoft 365 E5 should therefore use a separate, non-enrolled subscription to avoid duplicate charges. Creating a host pool in a new subscription enables the external-user workload to be isolated and enrolled for per-user access pricing.

**Learn more:** [Licensing Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/licensing) · [Enroll in per-user access pricing for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/enroll-per-user-access-pricing)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop pooled host pool named Pool1 in the East US Azure region.  
  
You create the scaling plans shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783893136203-pqh0ij2v.png)  
  
Which scaling plans can be assigned to Pool1?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Desktop scaling plan can be assigned only to host pools in the same Azure region and with a host-pool type that matches the plan. Pool1 is pooled and located in East US, so only SP2 meets both requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop pooled host pool named Pool1 in the East US Azure region.  
  
You create the scaling plans shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783893136203-pqh0ij2v.png)  
  
Which scaling plans can be assigned to Pool1?
questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access is available with Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2, which must be enabled for the subscription. Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 1 does not include this capability, so Plan 2 is the lowest-cost listed license that satisfies the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access) · [Overview of Defender for Servers in Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-servers-overview)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
An Azure Virtual Desktop deployment contains a host pool.  
  
The host pool has 100 session hosts running Windows 10 on general-purpose virtual machines.  
  
You plan to implement Quality of Service (QoS) for the deployment.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Switch to a high-performance computing (HPC) virtual machine.
Upgrade all the session hosts to Windows 11.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop QoS for RDP traffic is enabled through RDP Shortpath for managed networks. RDP Shortpath provides the direct UDP-based transport between the Remote Desktop client and session host and allows QoS policies to be configured for RDP data.\
\
**Learn more:** [Implement Quality of Service (QoS) for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-quality-of-service-qos)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: Add a private endpoint to storage1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Storage private endpoint lets clients in the virtual network access the Azure Files service through a private IP address. Traffic between the virtual-network clients and the storage account traverses the virtual network and Azure Private Link on the Microsoft backbone network, avoiding exposure to the public internet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints) · [Configure network endpoints for accessing Azure file shares](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-networking-endpoints)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: You configure virtual network peering for Vnet1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Virtual network peering only provides connectivity between virtual networks. It does not create a private endpoint for the Azure Files service in the storage account. Azure Private Link uses a private endpoint to route traffic between a virtual network and Azure Storage over the Microsoft backbone network.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints) · [What is Azure Private Link?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/private-link/private-link-overview)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: Create a routing table and associate it with VNet1.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Files connectivity over the Microsoft backbone is provided by an Azure Storage service endpoint or an Azure Private Endpoint. A user-defined route table does not create that service connectivity, and route tables are associated with subnets rather than directly with a virtual network.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview) · [Use private endpoints for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: Create a routing table and associate it with VNet1.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?

options.text: Assign the Desktop Virtualization Reader role for Pool1 to the users.
Modify the RDP Properties of Pool1.

questions.explanation:
Clipboard redirection between a remote session (including RemoteApp sessions) and the local device is controlled through the custom RDP property 'redirectclipboard:i:0', which is set on the host pool's RDP Properties (Device Redirection > Clipboard setting). Since App1 is published from RemoteAppGroup1, which is tied to Pool1, disabling clipboard redirection on Pool1's RDP Properties blocks copy-paste between the RemoteApp and the local device. AppLocker governs which applications can run, resource locks prevent deletion/modification of Azure resources, and the Desktop Virtualization Reader RBAC role only grants read access to AVD objects—none of these control clipboard redirection behavior.

**Learn more:** [Configure clipboard redirection over the Remote Desktop Protocol - Azure Virtual Desktop | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/redirection-configure-clipboard) · [Set custom RDP properties on a host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/customize-rdp-properties)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: In the Local Group Policy Editor, you configure the **Security settings**.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Automatically signing out disconnected Azure Virtual Desktop users requires the Remote Desktop Session Host policy **Set time limit for disconnected sessions** under **Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Session Time Limits**. Security settings do not configure this disconnected-session timeout.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan)

questions.explanation:

Remote Session Environment settings do not configure this session time limit. [Microsoft Learn: Start VM on Connect FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/start-virtual-machine-connect-faq#are-vms-automatically-deallocated-when-a-user-stops-using-them)\

questions.question:
Solution: In the Local Group Policy Editor, configure the **Session Time Limits** settings.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Remote Desktop Session Host policy **Set time limit for disconnected sessions**, located under **Session Time Limits**, can be enabled with a timeout and configured to end disconnected sessions. Ending the session signs out the user automatically after the configured disconnected-session limit.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan) · [Azure Virtual Desktop autoscale FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-faq)

questions.question:
Solution: Using the Local Group Policy Editor, you configure the **Connections** settings.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts automatically sign users out after disconnection only when the Remote Desktop Session Host policy **Set time limit for disconnected sessions** is configured under **Session Time Limits** and set to end the disconnected session. The **Connections** policy settings do not provide that disconnected-session sign-out configuration.\
\

questions.explanation:
Ephemeral OS disks create a non-persistent session-host environment. OneDrive sync support in non-persistent Azure Virtual Desktop requires the latest FSLogix installation, and the OneDrive sync app must be installed per machine so it is available consistently to all users rather than being installed in each user profile.

questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool in the US East Azure region.  
  
You need to ensure that the host pool can fail over to the US West Azure region.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Create a virtual machine snapshot of each session host.
Create an Azure Storage account that uses geo-redundant storage (GRS).

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop cross-region business-continuity designs use a separate host pool in the secondary region. In an active-passive design, another host pool is deployed in the secondary region, so creating the US West host pool establishes the required failover target.\
\
**Learn more:** [Business continuity considerations for Azure Virtual Desktop workloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/azure-virtual-desktop/business-continuity)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts created from a custom gallery image require a generalized image so that each new VM can receive its own machine-specific configuration. The image must also be available in the deployment region. Image1 is the only generalized image in West US.

**Learn more:** [Create an Azure Virtual Desktop golden image](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-golden-image) · [Deprovision or generalize a VM before creating an image](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/generalize)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and use Azure's **Start/Stop VMs during off-hours** feature.  
  
You need to specify which virtual machines the solution must never stop.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: the Diagnostic settings of the host pool

questions.explanation:
Start/Stop VMs during off-hours uses Azure Automation runbooks, and its exclusion configuration is maintained as Azure Automation account variables. Automation variables can store shared configuration values, including lists of virtual machine names, for use by runbooks.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage variables in Azure Automation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/shared-resources/variables)

You need to configure the virtual machines whose names begin with the Pool1 prefix so that the solution satisfies the technical requirements.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: an Azure Virtual Desktop automation task

questions.explanation:
The technical requirement specifies that the Pool1 virtual machines must run only during business hours, which requires both automatically starting and stopping the VMs on a recurring schedule. Azure Automation lets you create runbooks (such as the built-in Start/Stop VMs during off-hours solution) that start and stop VMs based on a defined schedule, fully satisfying this requirement while minimizing administrative overhead. VM auto-shutdown only supports a single scheduled shutdown time and cannot start the VMs again, Service Health in Azure Monitor is unrelated to VM power management (it reports on Azure service incidents/outages), and there is no Azure Virtual Desktop feature called an 'automation task'.

**Learn more:** [Exam AZ-140 topic 15 question 1 discussion - ExamTopics](https://www.examtopics.com/discussions/microsoft/view/64664-exam-az-140-topic-15-question-1-discussion/) · [Start/Stop VMs during off-hours overview - Azure Automation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-solution-vm-management)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment containing a pooled host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has five session hosts.  
  
You plan to deploy two applications named App1 and App2. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Both apps must be present on every session host.  
- Every user must connect to a full desktop session.  
- Only sales-department users must be able to use App1.  
- Only research-department users must be able to use App2.  
  
You need to ensure that users in each department see only their assigned app when they connect to Pool1.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
FSLogix application masking uses application rule sets that can hide applications for specified users or groups. It therefore lets both applications remain installed on every pooled-host-pool session host while sales and research users receive full desktops in which only their authorized application is visible and usable.

**Learn more:** [FSLogix Apps RuleEditor and Rule Sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/concepts-fslogix-apps-rule-editor-rule-sets) · [Create and Implement Rule Sets (Application Masking)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fslogix/tutorial-application-rule-sets)

questions.question:
Solution: On an Azure AD DS-joined computer, you modify the AADDC Users GPO settings.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
The **Set time limit for active but idle Remote Desktop Services sessions** policy is available under User Configuration, and Azure AD DS provides an AADDC Users GPO for the managed domain’s user container. Configuring the user-scoped session-timeout policy in that GPO applies the idle timeout to users who connect to the session hosts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Administer Group Policy in a Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/domain-services/manage-group-policy) · [ADMX_TerminalServer Policy CSP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-admx-terminalserver)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure portal, modify the **Session behavior** settings in the RDP Properties of Pool1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Idle-session timeouts are enforced through Remote Desktop Session Host session-time-limit policies on the session hosts, such as the policy to set a time limit for active but idle Remote Desktop Services sessions. Azure Virtual Desktop host-pool RDP Properties do not provide an idle-session-timeout setting.\
\
**Learn more:** [Supported RDP properties - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-properties) · [Set time limit for active but idle Remote Desktop Services sessions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/remote/remote-desktop-services/clients/rdp-files)

questions.domain: Plan and implement user environments and apps
questions.question:
Solution: From a computer joined to Azure AD DS, modify the **AADDC Computers GPO** settings.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD DS includes a built-in GPO for the AADDC Computers container, which contains computer objects joined to the managed domain. Its settings can be customized through Group Policy management from a domain-joined computer, allowing computer-based idle session timeout policies to apply to the session hosts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage group policy in Microsoft Entra Domain Services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/domain-services/manage-group-policy) · [Create an organizational unit (OU) in Microsoft Entra Domain Services](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-domain-services/create-ou)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: In the Azure portal, modify the **Advanced** settings under the RDP Properties of Pool1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An idle-session timeout is configured through the Remote Desktop Services **Set time limit for active but idle Remote Desktop Services sessions** policy. Host-pool Advanced RDP Properties configure RDP connection properties and do not set the session host’s idle-session time limit.\
\
**Learn more:** [ADMX_TerminalServer Policy CSP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-admx-terminalserver) · [Set custom RDP properties on a host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/customize-rdp-properties)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783807486561-uac6hw0d.png)  
  
You plan to deploy a new host pool as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783807489764-2d71pmu8.png)  
  
You need to ensure that the host pool can be deployed.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a lock to the existing host pool.
Stop and deallocate one of the currently deployed virtual machines.
Submit a support request for service and subscription limits.
Change the proposed virtual machine size for the session hosts to D4s_v3.

questions.explanation:
The existing deployment uses 40 of the 50 available West US regional vCPUs. Four D8s_v3 session hosts require 32 additional vCPUs, raising the total to 72 and exceeding the regional vCPU quota. Azure calculates VM quota for both allocated and deallocated cores, so stopping and deallocating an existing VM does not resolve the limit. Request an increase through Service and subscription limits.

**Learn more:** [vCPU quotas - Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/quotas) · [Request a quota increase using the Azure Support REST API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/support/quota-payload)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 that includes 10 session hosts.  
  
You have an app named App1 that uses the registry and creates files during installation.  
  
You plan to deploy App1 to Pool1.  
  
You need to create an App Attach package for App1.  
  
What should you use to create the package?

options.text: the Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop App Attach uses an MSIX-packaged application, which is subsequently expanded into an MSIX disk image. The MSIX Packaging Tool can capture and convert an installer that creates registry entries and files into an MSIX package; the MSIX Packaging Tool Environment provides the clean conversion environment for this process.

**Learn more:** [Create an MSIX package from any desktop installer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/msix/packaging-tool/create-app-package) · [Create an MSIX image to use with App Attach in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/app-attach-create-msix-image)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that uses Microsoft 365 cloud services, including Microsoft Teams.  
  
Users connect to the deployment from Windows 10 computers by using the Remote Desktop client.  
  
You need to enable audio and video in Azure Virtual Desktop and give users access to Microsoft Teams calling and meeting features.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Install the Microsoft Teams WebSocket Service on the Windows 10 computers
Configure the IsWVDEnvironment registry key on the Windows 10 computers
Configure the IsWVDEnvironment registry key on the virtual machines
Install the Microsoft Teams desktop app on the Windows 10 computers
Install the Microsoft Teams WebSocket Service on the virtual machines
Install the Microsoft Teams desktop app on the virtual machines

questions.explanation:
Teams media optimization for Azure Virtual Desktop requires configuring the `IsWVDEnvironment` DWORD registry value on each session host, installing the Teams WebSocket service (now represented by the WebRTC Redirector service) on each session host, and installing the Teams desktop app on the session-host virtual machines. These components enable optimized audio, video, calling, and meeting functionality within the virtual desktop session.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/teams-on-avd) · [Microsoft Teams for Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has two session hosts named Host1 and Host2.  
  
You need to enable screen capture protection for the deployment.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure a Group Policy setting on Host1 and Host2.
From RDP Properties for Pool1, disable Clipboard redirection.
Install an Azure virtual machine extension on Host1 and Host2.
From RDP Properties for Pool1, disable encoding of redirected video.

questions.explanation:
Screen capture protection is controlled by the **Enable screen capture protection** policy on Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts. Apply the relevant Group Policy setting to both Host1 and Host2. Clipboard redirection and redirected-video encoding are unrelated RDP redirection settings.\
\
**Learn more:** [Screen capture protection in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/screen-capture-protection)

questions.domain: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has two session hosts named Host1 and Host2.  
  
You need to enable screen capture protection for the deployment.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Deploy two Azure Firewall instances and Azure Firewall Manager.
Filter traffic by using outbound rules.
Filter traffic by using infrastructure rules.
Filter traffic by using inbound rules.
Deploy a network security group (NSG) and two application security groups.
Deploy an Azure Firewall instance and Azure Firewall Manager.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts need outbound connectivity to Azure Virtual Desktop service endpoints, while normal Azure Virtual Desktop operation does not require opening inbound ports. Azure Firewall can restrict and filter this outbound traffic. Azure Firewall Manager centrally deploys and configures multiple Azure Firewall instances across regions and subscriptions, supporting a distributed design while centrally managing its security policy.

**Learn more:** [Use Azure Firewall to protect Azure Virtual Desktop deployments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/protect-azure-virtual-desktop) · [What is Azure Firewall Manager?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall-manager/overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1 and an Azure Automation account named Account1. Pool1 is integrated with an Azure Active Directory Domain Services (Azure AD DS) managed domain named contoso.com.  
  
You plan to configure scaling for Pool1 by using Azure Automation runbooks.  
  
You need to authorize the runbooks to manage Pool1 scaling. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: a managed identity in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD)
a group Managed Service Account (gMSA) in Azure AD DS
a Connections shared resource in Azure Automation
a Run As account in Azure Automation

questions.explanation:
A managed identity for the Azure Automation account lets its runbooks authenticate to Azure resources without storing or maintaining credentials or certificates. Granting that identity the required RBAC permissions on the Azure Virtual Desktop and session-host resources authorizes scaling operations with minimal administrative overhead. Azure Automation Run As accounts have been retired and replaced by managed identities.

**Learn more:** [Azure Automation account authentication overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-security-overview) · [Set up scaling of session hosts using Azure Automation and Azure Logic Apps for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-scaling-script)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy the Azure Virtual Desktop host pools shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783893997606-wavxd52z.png)  
  
What is the maximum number of users who can connect simultaneously to the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment?
questions.explanation:
A pooled host pool’s maximum session limit is the maximum number of users load-balanced to each session host. Pool1 supports 5 × 6 = 30 users and Pool2 supports 3 × 5 = 15 users. A personal host pool has a maximum session limit of one user per session host, so Pool3 supports 15 users. The deployment therefore supports 60 simultaneous users.

**Learn more:** [Azure Virtual Desktop terminology](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/terminology) · [Configure host pool load balancing in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-load-balancing)

questions.domain: Plan and implement user environments and apps
questions.question:
You need to configure device-redirection settings. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
Where should the settings be configured?
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop device-redirection behavior is controlled by the host pool’s RDP properties. A workspace publishes resources, while user and Microsoft Entra groups control access rather than device redirection.

questions.domain: Plan and implement user environments and apps
questions.question:
Solution: From the host pool, you modify the Drain mode for Host1.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop drain mode blocks new user sessions on a session host and redirects new connections to another available host, while existing user sessions remain active until sign-out or administrative termination.\
\
**Learn more:** [Drain session hosts for maintenance in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/drain-mode)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: In Host1's virtual machine properties, enable just-in-time (JIT) VM access.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Just-in-time (JIT) VM access controls temporary inbound management access to a virtual machine; it does not prevent Azure Virtual Desktop from placing new user sessions on that session host. Azure Virtual Desktop drain mode blocks new sessions and leaves existing sessions active until users sign out or an administrator ends them.\
\
**Learn more:** [Drain session hosts for maintenance in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/drain-mode)

questions.domain: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: You remove Host1 from the session host list in the host pool.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Removing a session host is a deletion operation and may require forcing the deletion when user sessions exist. Drain mode is the appropriate maintenance control: setting `AllowNewSession` to `false` prevents new user sessions while existing connections remain active until users sign out or an administrator ends them.\
\
**Learn more:** [Drain session hosts for maintenance in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/drain-mode) · [Remove-AzWvdSessionHost (Az.DesktopVirtualization)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.desktopvirtualization/remove-azwvdsessionhost?view=azps-15.4.0)

questions.domain: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
questions.question:
Solution: In the virtual machine properties for Host1, you configure the Auto-shutdown settings.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop drain mode prevents a session host from accepting new user sessions while keeping existing sessions active until users sign out or an administrator ends them. Virtual machine Auto-shutdown shuts down the host and does not provide that non-disruptive session-host drain behavior.\
\
**Learn more:** [Drain session hosts for maintenance in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/drain-mode)

questions.domain: Plan and implement identity and security
questions.question:
Solution: Add a lock to Host1 from the Azure portal.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure resource lock does not prevent Azure Virtual Desktop from assigning new user sessions to a session host. Drain mode blocks new sessions and redirects new connections to another available session host while existing sessions remain active.\
\
**Learn more:** [Drain session hosts for maintenance in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/drain-mode)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool containing two session hosts. The Microsoft Teams client is installed on both session hosts.  
  
You find that only Microsoft Teams chat and collaboration features work; calling and meeting features are disabled.  
  
You need to ensure that users can configure calling and meeting features from within Microsoft Teams.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the Remote Desktop WebRTC Redirector Service.
Configure Remote audio mode in the RDP Properties.
Install the Teams Meeting add-in for Outlook.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop supports chat and collaboration by default, but calling and meeting functionality requires media optimization. The Remote Desktop WebRTC Redirector Service is the session-host component that enables this optimization and redirects media to the local device.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Teams on Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/teams-on-avd)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool that uses FSLogix user profiles. The user profiles are kept in an Azure Files share named share1.  
  
You need to back up share1 by using Azure Backup.  
  
What should you create first? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Backup protects Azure Files by using a Recovery Services vault. The vault must be in the same region and subscription as the storage account that hosts the file share, and it provides the backup management and recovery-point storage needed to configure protection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Back up Azure Files using Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/tutorial-backup-azure-files-vault-tier-portal)

What should you create first? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment and a Microsoft Entra Domain Services domain. The deployment includes 10 session hosts joined to the domain.  
  
You plan to deploy FSLogix profile containers and store those containers in Azure.  
  
You need to configure storage for the containers. The solution must ensure that you can assign share permissions to Microsoft Entra accounts.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Data storage settings of the storage account, enable an identity source.
Attach a new virtual disk to each session host.
From the Configuration settings of the storage account, select Default to Microsoft Entra authorization in the Azure portal.
Create a premium file shares storage account.
Create a premium block blobs storage account.

questions.explanation:
Azure Files supports identity-based SMB authentication through Microsoft Entra Domain Services. Enabling that identity source on the storage account permits Microsoft Entra Domain Services identities to receive Azure Files share-level permissions. Configuring the portal to default to Microsoft Entra authorization makes Microsoft Entra authorization the default data-access method in the Azure portal. Premium Azure Files is a performance and latency choice, not a prerequisite for Microsoft Entra-based share permissions.

**Learn more:** [Enable Microsoft Entra Domain Services authentication on Azure Files](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-identity-auth-domain-services-enable) · [Authorize access to Azure file share data in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/authorize-data-operations-portal)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You use Hyper-V to create a virtual machine that runs Windows 11 and has the following configuration:  
  
- Virtual machine generation: Generation 2  
- Disk type: Dynamically expanding  
- Disk format: VHDX  
- Disk size: 2 TB  
  
You need to prepare the virtual machine before you upload it to Azure.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Decrease the disk size to 1 TB.
Change the disk type to fixed.
Change the disk type to differencing.
Change the disk format to VHD.
Change the virtual machine generation to generation 1.

questions.explanation:
Azure supports both Generation 1 and Generation 2 virtual machines when their virtual disks use the VHD file format and are fixed-size disks. The dynamically expanding VHDX must therefore be converted to a fixed VHD. The VM generation should remain Generation 2, which Azure supports and which cannot be changed by converting the disk.

**Learn more:** [Prepare a Windows VHD or VHDX to upload to Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/sv-se/azure/virtual-machines/windows/prepare-for-upload-vhd-image)

You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment that includes two host pools named Pooll and Pool2.  
  
Pool1 contains 10 session hosts and supports 100 concurrent users. Pool2 contains two session hosts and supports 20 concurrent users.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure Virtual Desktop update solution that satisfies these requirements:  
  
- All service updates must be tested before they reach general availability.  
- Testing must have minimal impact on the organization.  
- No new host pools can be created.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: From the properties of Pool1, enable the validation environment.
From the properties of Pool2, enable the validation environment.
From the properties of Pool1, assign a scaling plan.
From the properties of Pool2, assign a scaling plan.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Virtual Desktop validation host pool receives service updates before non-validation environments, enabling them to be tested before broader release. Enabling the validation environment on Pool2 uses an existing host pool and limits the potential impact to the smaller pool, which supports 20 concurrent users rather than Pool1’s 100.

**Learn more:** [Configure a host pool as a validation environment - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-validation-environment)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription that includes an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named HostPool1. HostPool1 is managed by using Microsoft Intune. Subscription1 contains 50 users who connect to HostPool1 by using computers running Windows 10.  
  
You need to stop users from copying files between an Azure Virtual Desktop session and their computers. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Modify the RDP properties of HostPool1.
Create a Conditional Access policy in Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).
Create a compliance policy in Intune.
Create a configuration profile in Intune.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop host pool RDP properties control clipboard redirection for all connections to the host pool. Disabling clipboard redirection (`redirectclipboard:i:0`) makes the local clipboard unavailable in the remote session, preventing clipboard-based file transfers in either direction. This host-pool-level setting applies centrally and requires less administration than creating and deploying an Intune configuration profile.

**Learn more:** [Configure clipboard redirection over the Remote Desktop Protocol - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/redirection-configure-clipboard) · [Supported RDP properties - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-properties)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an on-premises Active Directory domain and an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The computer accounts for every session host are located in an organizational unit (OU) named WVDHostsOU. All user accounts reside in an OU named CorpUsers.  
  
A domain administrator creates a Group Policy Object (GPO) named Policy1 that contains only user settings. The administrator links Policy1 to WVDHostsOU.  
  
You find that, when users sign in to the session hosts, none of Policy1's settings are applied.  
  
What should you configure so that GPO settings apply to users when they sign in to the session hosts?
questions.explanation:
Loopback processing applies the user-configuration settings from GPOs assigned based on the session host computer’s OU, regardless of which user signs in. It therefore allows the user settings in Policy1, linked to WVDHostsOU, to apply during sign-in to those session hosts.

**Learn more:** [Group Policy processing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/group-policy/group-policy-processing)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783885651790-ikk62wcm.png)  
  
For which host pools can a load-balancing algorithm be configured?
questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop supports the breadth-first and depth-first load-balancing algorithms for pooled host pools. Personal host pools use a one-to-one user-to-session-host assignment and do not use these configurable algorithms. Therefore, the pooled host pools, Pool1 and Pool4, support a load-balancing algorithm.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure host pool load balancing in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-load-balancing)

You manage an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. The session hosts in Pool1 have a third-party application named App1 installed, which is published through a RemoteApp group.  
  
Each month, a new MSI-based version of App1 is installed on every host, and each version's executable file has a different name.  
  
You need to automate the process of publishing each new version of App1 through RemoteApp. The process must ensure that the user experience stays the same when the application is launched from the Windows Desktop client.  
  
Which two cmdlets should you run? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**(Choose two.)**
questions.explanation:
Because the executable file name changes with every monthly release, the existing RemoteApp application object (which stores the FilePath to the executable) becomes invalid and must be replaced. Remove-AzWvdApplication deletes the existing application entry from the RemoteApp application group, and New-AzWvdApplication then creates a new application entry pointing to the new executable's FilePath while reusing the same FriendlyName, IconPath, and CommandLineSetting values used previously — so the icon, display name, and launch behavior seen by users on the Windows Desktop client remain unchanged. This pair of cmdlets can be scripted to run automatically each month after the new MSI is installed. The MSIX package cmdlets do not apply because App1 is MSI-based, not an MSIX app attach package, and New-AzWvdApplicationGroup/New-AzRoleAssignment address group creation and access assignment, not updating an existing published application's target executable.

**Learn more:** [New-AzWvdApplication (Az.DesktopVirtualization) | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.desktopvirtualization/new-azwvdapplication) · [Remove-AzWvdApplication (Az.DesktopVirtualization) | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.desktopvirtualization/remove-azwvdapplication)

You have an Azure subscription containing a user named User1 and an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The deployment includes the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783906024911-u0u6s41l.png)  
  
You need to assign User1 to the Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
To which resources can you assign User1?
questions.explanation:
In Azure Virtual Desktop you grant users access by assigning them to application groups, so User1 can be assigned to AppGrp1 (in Pool1) and AppGrp2 (in Pool2). Because Pool2 is a personal host pool, you can additionally assign User1 directly to a specific session host (Host2) using 'Assign VM'. You cannot assign users to host pools themselves, and you cannot directly assign a user to an individual session host in a pooled host pool (Host1 in Pool1). The correct set is therefore Host2, AppGrp1, and AppGrp2 (C); option B is wrong because it lists a host pool (Pool2) and omits AppGrp1.

**Learn more:** [Configure personal desktop assignment in AVD](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-personal-desktop-assignment-type) · [Azure Virtual Desktop terminology](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/terminology)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network includes 20 Windows 10 devices.  
  
You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You need to deploy the Microsoft Remote Desktop client (MSRDC) to the devices. The MSRDC must be available to all users who sign in to the devices.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the MSRDC by using msiexec.exe and the ALLUSERS=1 command line option.
Install the MSRDC by using msiexec.exe and the ALLUSERS=2 command line option.
Install the MSRDC by using msiexec.exe and the MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1 command line option.

questions.explanation:
A per-device MSRDC installation makes the client available to all users of the computer. Microsoft specifies `msiexec` with `ALLUSERS=1` for a per-device installation; `ALLUSERS=2 MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1` installs per user.

**Learn more:** [Use features of the Remote Desktop client for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/remote-desktop-client/client-features-windows-msrdc) · [Installation Context](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/msi/installation-context)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment containing a pooled host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has four Microsoft Entra joined session hosts.  
  
Users report that, when attempting to sign in to a session host, they receive a message that their account is not configured to sign in.  
  
You need to assign users a role-based access control (RBAC) role so they can sign in to the session hosts. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to the users?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra joined Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts require users to have the Virtual Machine User Login RBAC role to sign in with standard user privileges. Virtual Machine Administrator Login provides unnecessary local administrator privileges, so it does not meet least-privilege requirements.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra joined session hosts in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/azure-ad-joined-session-hosts) · [Troubleshoot connections to Microsoft Entra joined VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/virtual-desktop/troubleshoot-azure-ad-connections)

Your company has one office and 40 employees.  
  
You are planning an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The estimated user workloads are shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783807458508-ld7z3ud4.png)  
  
Half of the users in each workload type work from home. All users who work from home do **not** establish a VPN connection to the office.  
  
Approximately how much bandwidth is required between the office and Azure to support the planned workloads?
questions.explanation: Only users working in the office consume the connection between the office and Azure. Their estimated bandwidth requirement is 10 light users × 1.5 Mbps, plus 5 medium users × 3 Mbps, plus 5 heavy users × 5 Mbps: 15 + 15 + 25 = 55 Mbps.

Azure Virtual Desktop QoS policies for RDP data are supported through RDP Shortpath for managed networks, which provides the required direct UDP-based transport. questions.question:
An Azure subscription contains an Azure Virtual Desktop session host named Host1 and a user named User1.  
  
You need to assign Host1 as a personal desktop for User1.  
  
Which cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
Update-AzWvdSessionHost assigns a user to an Azure Virtual Desktop personal session host by setting the session host’s `AssignedUser` value. Microsoft’s Azure Virtual Desktop guidance shows this cmdlet with the `AssignedUser` parameter for personal desktop assignment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure personal desktop assignment in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/configure-host-pool-personal-desktop-assignment-type)

questions.explanation:
A shared access signature (SAS) provides delegated, granular access to Azure Storage. It can be limited to the required Azure Files resource, operations, and time period, whereas a storage account access key provides broad access to the entire storage account.

**Learn more:** [Grant limited access to Azure Storage resources using shared access signatures (SAS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview) · [Securing PaaS applications using Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/paas-applications-using-storage)

You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing 200 users. Each user has a Microsoft 365 Apps for business license.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure Virtual Desktop personal host pool for 50 users. The planned deployment will use the following configuration:  
  
- A dedicated virtual machine will be assigned to every user.  
- Every virtual machine will run Windows 11 and have Microsoft 365 apps installed.  
  
You need to recommend a licensing solution for the deployment that minimizes costs.  
  
Which license type should the recommendation include?

options.text: Remote Desktop Services client access licenses (RDS CALs)

questions.explanation:
Windows 11 Enterprise E3 is an eligible per-user license for accessing Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts running Windows 11 Enterprise. Microsoft 365 Apps for business covers the Microsoft 365 apps, but it does not provide the required Windows Enterprise/AVD access entitlement. RDS CALs are the licensing path for Windows Server session hosts, while Microsoft Entra ID P2 does not provide Windows virtual desktop access rights. Microsoft 365 F3 is a frontline-worker offering and cannot be assumed appropriate for unspecified general users.

**Learn more:** [Licensing Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/licensing) · [Windows Enterprise E3 in CSP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/windows-enterprise-e3-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You deploy Azure Virtual Desktop.  
  
Which two Azure Virtual Desktop features require assigning Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) roles to the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Autoscale requires an Azure RBAC role on the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal so the service can manage the power state of session-host VMs. App Attach requires RBAC role assignment to the Azure Virtual Desktop service principals when Azure Files is used with Microsoft Entra ID-joined session hosts. Azure Virtual Desktop Insights requires roles for the people who configure or view monitoring data, not this service-principal assignment.

**Learn more:** [Assign Azure RBAC roles or Microsoft Entra roles to the Azure Virtual Desktop service principals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/service-principal-assign-roles) · [Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/autoscale-create-assign-scaling-plan)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a hybrid Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) and Microsoft Entra ID environment with 1,000 users.  
  
You plan to deploy Azure Virtual Desktop. The session host virtual machines will join the AD DS domain. Each session host will support five concurrent user sessions running Microsoft 365 apps.  
  
You need to choose the image for the planned Azure Virtual Desktop deployment. The solution must minimize licensing costs.  
  
Which image should you use for the deployment?
questions.explanation:
Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session supports multiple concurrent users on a single Azure Virtual Desktop session host and is optimized for pooled, multi-user scenarios that reduce the number of required virtual machines and operating-system overhead. Microsoft documents Windows 10/11 multi-session as the recommended image type for pooled host pools and notes its cost-reduction benefit for Azure Virtual Desktop.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Virtual Desktop?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/overview) · [Create an Azure Virtual Desktop golden image](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/set-up-golden-image)

You have an Azure subscription named Sub1.  
  
Sub1 contains an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment with a host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has five session hosts in the West Europe Azure region.  
  
You plan to implement an active-active disaster recovery solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Users must be able to connect only to session hosts in either the West Europe or North Europe Azure region.  
- Users must have only one workspace in the Remote Desktop client.  
  
Which two actions should you take to deploy the session hosts in the North Europe region? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create five virtual machines in the North Europe region.
Configure Azure Site Recovery to replicate the session hosts of Pool1.
Create a new host pool named Pool2 and add the five virtual machines from the North Europe region as session hosts.
From Pool1, add the five virtual machines from the North Europe region as additional session hosts.

questions.explanation:
An active-active Azure Virtual Desktop deployment uses two host pools, one in each region. Five virtual machines must be created in North Europe and registered as session hosts in a new North Europe host pool. The host pools can publish resources through a single workspace, while Azure Virtual Desktop manages the connection brokering without a cross-region load balancer.

**Learn more:** [Multiregion BCDR for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/example-scenario/azure-virtual-desktop/azure-virtual-desktop-multi-region-bcdr) · [Business continuity considerations for Azure Virtual Desktop workloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/azure-virtual-desktop/business-continuity)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop host pool named Pool1. Pool1 has one session host, named Host1.  
  
You need to ensure that a user is automatically signed out when an Azure Virtual Desktop session has been inactive for 30 minutes. The solution must **not** affect other session timeout settings.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, configure the Security & privacy settings.
From Host1, run the Set-ItemProperty cmdlet.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, create and assign a Conditional Access session policy.
From the Local Group Policy Editor on Host1, modify the Remote Desktop Services settings.

questions.explanation:
Remote Desktop Services session time-limit policies on the session host include a setting for active but idle sessions. Configuring that policy to 30 minutes, together with ending the session when the limit is reached as required, applies the idle-session behavior independently of the disconnected-session and active-session timeout settings. Microsoft documents these policies under Remote Desktop Session Host > Session Time Limits.

**Learn more:** [ADMX_TerminalServer Policy CSP](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-admx-terminalserver)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Virtual Desktop deployment.  
  
You need to enable USB-drive redirection to the virtual machines. The solution must ensure that every USB drive is accessible.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure the RDP properties of the host pool.
Install the Remote Desktop WebRTC Redirector Service on the session hosts.
Configure the local Group Policy settings of the session hosts.
Install Windows App on user devices.

questions.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop uses the host pool’s RDP properties to control USB device redirection. Configuring the USB device redirection property to redirect all supported USB devices makes all eligible USB drives available in the remote session.

**Learn more:** [Configure USB redirection on Windows over the Remote Desktop Protocol - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/redirection-configure-usb) · [Supported RDP properties - Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/rdp-properties)
